Wow, I don't think I have ever played a game that is this emotionally charged. I'll get more into that later, for now let's talk about the game in general.
Admittedly, the gameplay isn't really anything special, it isn't a lot more than your standard Third Person Shooter. It does contain some interesting mechanics involving the sand that is everywhere in Dubai. It isn't a very long game, but its main attraction is the story. It does take a little while for the story to really get intense but it is worth the wait. The events that take place in the story, as well as the way the game tries to make you feel bad about what you are doing is amazing. Also, be warned, the game contains some fairly graphic looking things at a few stages, but if you are playing a shooting game, it probably won't bother you.
The game will place moral choices in front of you more than a couple of times throughout its length. They all carry weight on you and your character, these aren't just your typical "give the object to person A or person B", you are playing with peoples lives in these decisions.
The game takes a fairly obvious anti-war stance, showing what can happen when things go really out of control. It is a need perspective that not a whole lot of games really take advantage of.
The PC port works great, never had any issues on the 760 I was using when I played it. It is a pretty nice looking game.
There is a multiplayer portion to the game, I don't know a lot about it because it isn't very populated, but from what I've read, it's a standard team based multiplayer portion. Like most of this game, it isn't very unique.
If you are on the fence about this game, it usually dips pretty cheap during seasonal sales, so get it then. It is absolutely worth that. There aren't many games that I feel I would be happy spending 60 dollars on, this is absolutely one of them.

Prison architect is a prison simulator with a grid building system and an in depth prisoner needs system.
Prison architect starts with the player immediately thrown into the game with hardy any tutorial. The real tutorial is the campaigns objectives. Once the player starts a game, they start with a small sum of money and must build a prison with the tools at their disposal. The player will build buildings for various rooms such as dormitories, cells, canteens, staff rooms, storage and other such necessities for the future prisoners and staff.
The prisoners come in all shapes and sizes, as well as various security levels; minimum, medium and high security. These prisoners act like real prisoners, if there is a shortage of food, a heat wave, power outages, or even a death can cause a riot to break out. Prisoners can be kept happy by having visitation rooms, recreational rooms, time in the yard, or an increase in variety of food. Should a riot break out, riot police and firefighters are available to help put them back in line, and medical centres or morgues are available for the wounded or fatalities.
Prison architect also has variety of options available when starting anew map, you can have weather as a factor, chose to have a large or small starting map, with our without trees, lakes or pre-existing buildings. Events are an interesting option, which can range from a power generator exploding, or a massive amount of prisoners arriving from another prison. Gangs can be turned on, which makes riots happen often, and if a gang leader is sent to your prison, the gangs can increase in size, and have wars over territory. Fog of war seems to be the most notorious of options. It prevents the player from seeing any prisoner unless a guard or camera is in the room, making it difficult, for the player to spot assaults or other such crimes.
Overall prison architects objective is to rehabilitate prisoners through reform programs, such as school, culinary or workshop programs. These, if passed, provide the prisoner with valuable work skills reducing the chance of reoffending, boosting your prison grade.
Prison architect does have a few things wrong with it.
Some lag when laying wires or pipes on lower grade PCs
Lack of realism in the riots or fighting
Slow to start for new players
The "campaign" lacks real story or drive
The names and descriptions of prisoners don't fit the actual crimes
Prison architect does a lot right.
Has a fantastic workshop
Has relatively easy achievements
Satisfying game
Has a surprisingly fun escape mode
Art and sound design are solid
Good animations
Fantastic in-depth needs system
Is prison architect worth the $32.99CAD? If you enjoy city builder type games, pick it up. Honestly if it goes on sale everyone should get it for their collection

Tiny Bang Story is primarily a hidden object game. The good things it has going for it are that the soundtrack is good, the hidden object gameplay is relaxing and satisfying, and the art is absolutely amazing. The art is very reminiscent of Amanita Design (e.g. Samarost, Machinarium).
One important thing to note about Tiny Bang Story that will make it or break it for you, though, is that the hidden object gameplay is periodically broken up by actual puzzles you have to solve or mini-arcade games where you have to navigate a pixel boat or airplane through some pixel trees and rocks, etc. These little puzzles and mini-games add more flavor and variety to the game, so on one hand they are welcome. On the other hand, the little atari-style mini games are not very fun, and they go on for what seems like an excessively long time, and if you make one mistake, you have to start the whole tedious thing over again. The puzzles are usually of the jigsaw or tangram variety, but there are some permutation or mathematical puzzles in there as well. At first these are very light and easy, but by the time you make it to the third or fourth area of the world, they suddenly become way more demanding and can be very cumbersome (I especially disliked the puzzle where you have to balance the luggage on the scales). This is especially true if you are primarily interested in the hidden object gameplay. You may find yourself wanting to just look up the solution so you can get back to searching for hidden objects and avoid being obstructed by these.
The game also has a hint system, which you can activate by swatting a bunch of flies until you fill up a hint meter, but in my experience, there were 2 or 3 situations where I pressed the hint button and it either did not give any hint at all (literally did nothing) or it gave me an absolutely useless hint, essentially telling me what my objective is or some other such information I already know.
Overall it seems like a pretty good game. I enjoyed the art and music, and I enjoyed how relaxing and warm it is. I personally felt the puzzles and mini-games got to be too cumbersome after a certain point, so I've lost my interest in finishing it, but it will be a very good game for the right kind of person.

Positives :
1- Its very cute and charming
2- The music is relaxing
3- Puzzles can be interesting in a passtime way
Negatives
1- Too many hidden object goals, with some being utterly camouflaged and/or incredibly tiny. These are required.
2- Jigsaw puzzles are long, annoying and frustating. On top of it, the music decided to stop so I quit.
3- The hint system is dumb - you have to click flies over and over and over and over... why? just... why?
4- Complete lack of story.
5- Perfect for an iPad ; for the kids to have a clickfest and look for the things together while in the car. On PC though, it just doesn't work - besides theres much more fun things to play.
Play Machinarium instead. This isn't even worth the dollar, even less your precious time, UNLESS you have kids that love silly puzzles.

They are entirely unlike the other puzzles in the game which are more cerebral and less... stupid. I wish they could be skipped. That being said there are only two of them, but they almost made me give up on the game.
Two, the transition between stages is really really bad. You have to collect all these puzzle pieces, and I was going to commend the game for designing it so that I had actually already found all the puzzle pieces before I completed the level and didn't need to spend time scouring for them (there's enough of that in the game anyway) but it turns out you don't actually need to find them all; for the 3rd stage I progressed without having all the puzzle pieces.
Either way, you have to do this jigsaw of the world between stages, and it's frankly, awful filler. Jigsaw games exist, and I wnjoy them, but what sets this one apart and brings it to a transendant level of awfulness is that maybe 20% of the pieces are sky, and while that's fine, sky has some texture to it... nope, the puzzle pieces are rendered with bloom on them that makes it impossible to read any subtle indicators.
To make the complaints of the transitions sucking a triqueta, I should also point out that the game locks up for a few seconds between stages, making me worried it will crash before I can put the puzzle pieces together.

Batman is always great. This one has stunning visuals, satisfying and brutal combat with well paced action. The story seems great, the gadgets are fun, and there is a whole city awaiting your justice.

While not quite rivaling its predecessors in quality, this is still a fairly good game. The plot is actually very creative and the first half is mainly oriented on Batman's detective skills, a welcome addition. While a few small tweaks to combat can ruin it on Hard difficulty, if you play on lesser difficulties, it shouldn't be an issue. Predator mode on the other hand, gains a few small gadget-based changes that are quite nice. In regards to the multiplayer, the idea is actually a very good one, but is hampered greatly by terrible latency, resulting in a less-than-optimal experience.
Unfortunately, those are not the only negatives, particularly the numerous bugs that still persist after their several patches. While a few are merely cosmetic, there are a few which can hamper combat or require a re-load of your save, impacting the overall enjoyment of the game.
While I recommend playing this if you enjoyed Arkham City, I wouldn't get it for more than $20-30, as there isn't enough new content to justify a higher price.

As far as RPG maker games go, this one has a special place in my heart. One that I enjoy the most.
It's charming on its own way, very compact and satisfying. Doesn't seem to try to go too far from what it can actually do.
I've only played the first episode so this might not be true for the second.
For me, the pros are:
>Combat, unlike many of its genre, feels interesting enough to keep me playing for quite some time. Even though it relies on random encounters (which can be avoided if you're fast enough), it doesn't feel irritating. I like how characters compliment each other with their abilities.
>Character customization, the passive skills are interesting and useful.
>Soundtrack is very fitting.
>Although the plot is generic, I enjoy the interaction between characters.
And the cons:
>Some NPCs have their walk cycles set to random and will sometimes block your path, since the mapping is very small and often you only have a single tile to walk through.
>May seem too difficult at first, some classes are clearly better at the start than others.
>Experience gain is very slow. I've got to about level 15 in 5 hours which makes the game kind of static.
For its price (got it on sale) it feels competent enough if you enjoy the genre.

This review is about Heroes of Legionwood Act 1: Age of Darkness and Act 2: Ressurection.
Both are purchased separately and so in all reality the full game (including all three acts) costs closer to $20-24
I bought this game on sale so bought it for closer to $3 and so I can't really complain.
This is my first type of rpgmaker game and so I have no experience with other games of the same type.
Pros:
-Choice of dialogue (Well you can choose the tone at least)
-Some replayability.
-The option to avoid random encounters entirely with the right item, which with it brought a blessing and a curse, which was interesting.
-Romance option (Though I didn't delve into it)
-Ability to start anew or continue on from an old save, I haven't tried starting anew and so don't know how character stats are determined.
-It does look nice
-Ability to get jobs (Though I never saw how many there were)
-The lore was quite interesting and I enjoyed the little tid bits, it could have been a bit longer, but looking at the reviews for Legionwood 1 and complaints of lore being shoved in your face it is quite understandable why there isn't a load of lore.
-Not too difficult on normal play (Though if you don't pay attention you may very well find yourself dead very quickly), though the game could be very difficult initially in hard difficulty
Neutral
-About 20 hours of play, the game does seem quite short, and yes this is understandable to avoid repetition but entering into the 3rd episode I won't have felt a lot of time has passed, the game feels like it could be easily be expanded on afterwards (Legionwood 3?)
- I would personally recommend waiting for all three episodes to come out so you can play them in succession
- NPCs do judge your decisions but it doesn't feel like it happens very much, it would be nice to people able to talk to them and just see how they are doing rather than having a few short scenes of them discussing their views.
-Enemies seem a bit repetitive
-Puzzles, I enjoyed the tiles puzzle but I would have liked to have had more of a challenge, I understand there could be complaints about puzzles being too hard, but maybe just having some optional harder puzzles to challenge the mind would have been cool.
-A bug
-A few unanswered questions
-The two acts can be played separately but watching the first act tells you important details that would affect your decisions in the second
Cons:
-In Episode 2 the "Quests" option in the menu disappears and so it is difficult to know what you are meant to do at times (i.e I stumbled upon the precursor key)
-I don't know the feel of other rpg games and I understand it isn't made from absolute scratch and resources are a bit limited, but I did feel that the traps were very repetitive (Only one form of "visual" trap in the game)
-Battles do get quite repetitive
If it's on sale again (Probably another degica sale) then I would definitely recommend buying it. But until the third episode comes out, it may not be necessarily be as fun as it could be.
Overall it was fun and I will enjoy playing the third episode, but I do hope that it answers a lot of questions and doesn't leave the game feeling too short, it will also be interesting to see how all my decisions affect the outcome, and if in light of that there will be a lot more replay-ability (With multiple endings?). Due to the fact I haven't played other similar games I can't really compare it to anything so to those who have played games of a similar type/genre this may not mean a lot to you.
If you're still not sure just try the demo I guess
Otherwise I hope this review was helpful.

Title : Euro Truck Simulator 2
Developer : SCS Software
Publisher : SCS Software
Genre : Simulator
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a vehicle simulation game. The game is a direct sequel of Euro Truck Simulator and it is the second video game in the Euro Truck Simulator series. The player can drive one of a choice of articulated trucks across a depiction of Europe, picking up cargo from various locations and delivering it. As the game progresses, it is possible for the player to buy more vehicles, depots, and hire drivers to work.
Players choose their HQ's location in any of the game map's cities. At first, the player can only take what are known as Quick jobs—these jobs involve making hired driver deliveries while employed by a delivery company, with a provided truck and all expenses (fuel, road tolls, ferry crossings) covered. As the player earns money or takes bank loans, they can eventually afford to buy themselves a truck, acquire a home garage, and start making more money by delivering cargo using their own truck instead of just being a driver for hire. Money earned in the game can be spent on upgrading or purchasing new trucks, hiring NPC drivers to take on deliveries, buying more garages and expanding the home garage to accommodate more trucks and drivers.

Brilliant asset to the COD series. This game did not disappoint when it came to frames per second, graphics, singleplayer and multiplayer gameplay. The upgraded Nuketown is excellent, and the detail is a job well done by Treyarch. Each map has its own unique voice, as well as each weapon. The DLC's weren't and still aren't so expensive, and they are quite the lookers for those who are willing to buy DLC's. I also liked the fact that this game has full controller support, as well as not glitching with console porting. Job well done Treyarch.
Singleplayer:
- Its the complete opposite of Black Ops 1, you now play as Mason's son.
- Well directed.
- I found some minor bugs though in the 4th mission.
- It was a tad predictable, but other than that, it was an average campaign, I personally finished it around 5 times.
Multiplayer:
- Maxium frames per second on my system: 325. (core i5 6400k@2.7GHz, sapphire radeon HD 7700, 8GB Corsair Gaming RAM)
- Well thought achievements on weapon upgrading.
- Maps have excellent detail.
- New assests to emblem creations.
- However, the community is a tad rough for those who just want to enjoy a nice quiet game of COD after a long day.
- Good-looking DLC's
- Good-looking unlockable Camo's.
All in all, I would recommend this game to the COD fans, and I'll rate it 7.5/10.

ATS has since come out, but I found that it wasn't as good as the original ETS2. The two DLCs - Going East! and Scandinavia - add large segments and map variation to the game, which I welcome. There is also a fairly accurate sense of distance and landscape, slightly shrunken down, with the average distance from Aberdeen to Bratislava taking about 2.5/3 hours real time. There are lots of truck paint job DLCs and cabin accessories, but only found myself buying these in Steam Summer Sales as they were no more than 20p each at the time. With the radio, though, I still sometimes tolerate long journeys listening to Antenne Dusseldorf of Magic London.
By far the best simulator, ETS2 will always be a favourite, with long-distance lorry driving being odly theraputic.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is probably the most realistic trucking simulator I've played. Realistic traffic AI, Real Trucks(Other than Majestic that was replaced with Mercedes recently), very long distance driving, realistic fatigue and air brake simulation(can be turned off), the game is very very good.
At launch the game had horrendous optimisation in areas of the map, even on high end PCs. They've patched this recently with the new rendering engine.. however there are a few problems that still exist:
Cons:
- * While in the drivers seat the cabin is unoptimised when you have the dash light or head lights turned on which results in a FPS loss(10-15 FPS on my rig).
-*Lights are still unoptimised.
-* On GNU/Linux systems with multi-monitor setups, the game ALWAYS uses the monitor furthest to the left. It's irritating. In my setup I have a 1440x900 on the left, 1440x900 on the right, and a 1920x1200 in the middle. The game will not see any resolution > 1440x900 despite the middle one being primary, and it refuses to enter fullscreen on any monitor except the one furthest to the left.
- * While turning corners sometimes your trailer gets stuck even when the tire just is scraping on the curb.
- * Trucks and Buses on single lane roads go half the speed limit(not really a con, but kind of annoying)
- * Speed limit signs are far too close, and change to rapidly. Sometimes you'll see a sign that says 90, then maybe not even half a KM later you get another sign that says 70 or 50. There are some parts where the speed limit drops from 130 down to 50 followed by a speed a camera meters a head.. WTF?
- * Most powerful engine available is 750 HP, and even then it's fairly slow while hauling a load. But thanks to mods that can be changed.

Charming game. Cute art, nice relaxing music.
Your mission is to put the world back together by finding all the puzzle pieces from each level to puzzle together the next one until you've finished building the world. A casual playthrough takes a bit more than 2 hours.
Some hidden objects can be quite hard to find/see. Imo the hint button recharges too slowly. You need to click 20ish flies on the screen for them to fill up to give you a hint charge. I don't mind games being hard, but this is just inconsistent with the relaxing, casual feel I get from the rest of the game.
The minigames are mostly fairly easy. The computer game simulating games are really frustrating though. Extremely slow, I ended up killing myself more than once by crashing into walls because the little ship/plane was so slow.
The jigsaw puzzle at the end of each level a have too many pieces. I quite like jigsaw puzzles, but it just takes too long and I lose interest and get bored of it.
You have to discover the puzzles to be able to pick up the items needed for them, like Morphopolis, which isn't too much of a problem as they're mostly obvious and easy to find.
Overall worth buying if you're into point&click/hidden object games, but be aware of a few frustrating elements.

I love it, it could have had better sidequests if it learnt from the witcher 3, and it's a shame it lacks motorbikes. But otherwise I struggle to fault it. It looks amazing, easlily runs over 100fps, the artwork and world creation is breathtaking,
Vehicular combat is super fun. and in depth, during convoy chases, all the particle effects and car damage look amazing and none of it creates any slow-down, even during an epic lightning sandstorm!
The combat has good weight and physics with epic animations including some super OP WWE finishers, Overall it's similar to the arkham batman combat, yet I belive better, in that Max doesn't skate around and ping between enemies like a pinball machine. instead you need to think about distance, positioning, and dodges, and timing much more.
If at first fuel, water, and scrap seem hard to get, focus on building up a stronghold, so that they start working for you and it all becomes automated and easy. leaving you more time to enjoy epic car chase battles :D
Oh, and the free-cam screenshot editor is a great feature, that you can easily access even during car chases for some epic camera angles and photo effects.

Terraria is a voxel based, open world sandbox game which involves building and combat. As Minecraft is mainly building, this game is mainly combat. Pretty much any computer can run it which is good and it offers plenty to do. There are countless blocks and countless weapons, and many many bosses to face. There is no real grind element to this game, other than gearing up to face the next boss in the sequence.
I would Highly recommend Terraria to anyone that enjoys single player games as there is countless things to do and monsters/bosses to kill. A very interesting and often challenging game which does not disappoint in any way.

Verdict: I highly recommend this game, despite its DRM and Voice Acting/Immersion flaws, this game makes up for it in a lot of ways, especially when you are looking at it with a 50% off price tag, if you are a fan of the Hitman Franchise or like myself, a fan of Hitman Blood Money but not Absoultion, this game will revive your faith in the series.
Pros:
+ This game has an amazing amount of replayability. After every level you complete you are given the option(s) to go back and use new starting areas, uniforms, and new targets to kill. And these new targets are updated almost weekly.
+ They went back to the game being more of a sandbox feel, like in Hitman Blood Money, which was sorely missed in Hitman Absolution
+ Once again Hitman delivers an incredible storyline, you aren't just killing nameless, stakeless, npc's but people who's deaths really contribute to the plot of the story.
Cons:
- The voice acting, this isn't a terrible negative about the game but it is annoying that they employ the same 4-5 voice actors throughout the entire game. It does not matter if you are in Sapienza, Marrakesh, or Hokkaido, everyone sounds like the same vanilla, mid-western accent; which kind of ruins the immersions.
- Online DRM, what I mean is that even though it is a single player game, you will always be connected online. Even if you have a strong connection you are ultimatley at the mercy of the Hitman servers, if they go down, you lose all progess if you had no saved.

An absolutely charming and elegant point-and-click puzzle game. Not much depth and nothing too tricky, but very absorbing and clever. Lots of little surprises to find, and a nice overall art direction. I wish there were more games out there like it!

I'm generally not the biggest fan of hidden object games, but if the hidden objects serve a sensible purpose, such as being part of an overall puzzle and leading to a variety of in-game puzzles, as they do in The Tiny Bang Story, I am wiling to spend a few hours playing through it.
The Tiny Bang Story has a pleasant and charming hand-drawn art style, hidden objects, and a range of mostly very casual puzzles, a few of which I found enjoyably tricky too. A puzzle game with no real challenges can easily get a bit too casual and thus boring.
Speaking of art style, I also enjoyed how some objects on the screen react to the mouse pointer, such as cables and lines shifting when you move over them. Quite nice. Though subtle, it makes the scene feel so much more alive.
There are in-game hints, with a clever and original time-delay between hints that seem to require a certain number of flies to be clicked on before a new one becomes available. Depending on what section you're in, a hint will either show you something you should be clicking on the screen, or it gives a solution hint to one of the puzzle games. It's simply nicely done.
The music is nice, downbeat and in the background, well suited for a game that requires focus such as this one, though it did start feeling a bit repetitive after a while - as music does in most games.
There is only one thing missing from this game, and that is decent video options to make it other than its original pixel dimensions. As I sometimes have to do this with older games anyway, it wasn't much bother for me just changing my screen's resolution through the control panel to suit the game.
In the end, I think it took me a bit less than 3.5 hour playing through the whole game, though with a few distractions along the way that probably kept me from doing it at optimum efficiency. At its current RRP, I think it is very decent value for money. On sale, or in a bundle, it should be mandatory shopping for anyone who loves puzzle games or even for those who just enjoy the art style.

If you buy this game, you may just be serving a sentence of your own...as time slips by, engroused in what you are doing. It's a fantastic managment, builder where the unpredictability of the prisoners (and pretty much everything else!) always has you interested.
The Pros:
- Just one more thing: Oh how mnay times I've thought "I'll just finish this bit and then I'll quit...no, wait, I'll do this bit too before I forget....oh and..."
- Organised Chaos: Prisoners are fun to watch, can be easy or difficult to manage. I've built only 3 or four prisons (early access) and have had everything from zero problems almost at all, to a riot that started literally 3 seconds after I accidently overpowered my electricity generator (leaving one gaurd dead and many prisoners bloody and unconscious!).
- Loads of space to build
- lots of info and lots to do. There's always plenty to do and work on.
- It's just damn fun and a good amouont of challenge
Take or leaves:
- Graphics: I like them, you should not be out off by them. There is a 3D mode, but it dodn't do much for me and I prefer the original personally
- Prisoner mode: you can be one of the prisoners and try to escape your own or anyone else's who have shared it in the Steam workshop. It was ok when I tried it but no real sense of actually living in the prison from what I tried. A hit and giggle feature but maybe I need to check it out again.
Cons:
- The tutorial and general information on how to actually play and whatthings do is very much NOT clear. I played the campaign tutorial a few times after extended breaks away from the game when it was in early access and I have avoided it this time around since its official release, so it may have been improved. But overall, you will almost certainly need to look up wikis and how to's, often for very simple thing. Thankfully, there is loads of community help and a working answer is easily found.
- Randomness that could be bugs or just lack of info: Sometimes you don't know why things are not working. Sometimes there are unclear clues, other times you 'll be cratching your heads (I have a few armed gaurds and security gaurds that gather together every night in the yard for no apparent reason. They are not scheduled to patrol there, but they do it anyway).
Really though, I find when I have a go at this game, I am sucked in for many long running sessions. Enough depth to satisfy a passionate builder/manager, not too much as to overwhelm. Eg, there are things like circuits and pressure plates, but you most definitely don't NEED them to run a prison (but it would help of course).
Very much recommended.

The gameplay is nothing special, it is in fact just another cover shooter in that respect. But this game's story is unparalleled by any other shooter, let alone cover shooter. It's a psychological tale that will test you.

The controls can be a hassle at times. Playing on a higher difficulty can be frustrating as the cover system is a bit wonky and you can hardly turn while sprinting making it hard to get into cover while doing so; annoying when the sprint button is the same as the cover button.

One of the most frustrating games I have ever played in my entire life.
Trial-and-error gamepaly ala Hotline Miami will keep you guessing and trying new things, dying over and over until you finally figure out the exact way to beat one of this game's umpteen million levels, not even taking into account the bonus bandage collectables for character unlocks and trying to ace the score every time (which is just an arbitrary A+ if you beat the par time, which in and of itself seems a bit pointless seeing as how there is actually no real grading system in the game.)
The dark world segments are duplicates of most of the vanilla levels, either slightly or dramatically tweeked to make the level even harder than it was your first time beating it, meaning all the memorising and careful planning was just pointless and next thing you know you are just begging for mercy from the evil hard videogame god. Bottom line, they are just complete and utter what in the hell, which is just glorious. And trying to climb the leaderboards is pointless, like with every game, thanks to some creative hacker gents.
But all-in-all, this game is just a spectacle to behold, much like the freakshow of a travelling circus, and you will marvel at just how rage-inducingly hard this game is. If you need a couple of hours to go by in a flash and completely for get about life for a while, this is the game for you.
P.S. Try not to ragequit, but no-one will blame you if you do...

Unfortunately, there is a 'wrong' and a 'right' way to play Boring Lands 2. I played through this game with a friend and we slowly got the notion that the game was getting too easy for us. Turned out that if you do all the side-quests on your first play-through, you'll eventually out-level everything else and fights just becoming a mind-numbing click fest as you plough through hordes of enemies with little to no effort.
In order to combat the drudgery, we altered our save games to give us access to a higher difficulty level at around level 25 and just started playing that. At first the challenge was amusing but then it just become a boring grind. Some enemies were too easy and others had far too much health and our weapons just couldn't really compete so we ended up using the Golden Keys to balance out the game. The Golden Keys were way too overpowered when we played on 'normal' and we swore not to use 'm because they were making the game even easier. On top of that, I picked the Mecromancher class which puts the game into easy-mode overdrive.
Although this game has a great sense of humour and good FPS mechanics, it has horrible balancing which completely ruined it for us. It is unforgiveable that players have to modify the game in order to face more of a challenge or simply not play parts of it because everything you do, ends up making the game easier.
On top of that, they actuall sell a Game Of The Year-edition that doesn't actually contain all of the DLC. That kind of renders the whole point of buying the GOTY moot as you'll still have to sift through the DLC list to find out what you might want.
Apparently overly simple FPS games is what the public wants nowadays. Cryin' shame.

I mistakenly avoided this game thinking it was a lame movie tie-in but after reading so many good reviews about it I gave in and tried it and I'm glad I did.
Gameplay wise it's a fusion of Just Cause, Far Cry and Shadows of Mordor.. A free roaming, base destroying, action packed adventure with a story to follow if you wish.
You start off with a basic car which you can scavenge parts for to upgrade, like a ram, harpoon or V8 engine etc etc

The most fun is from the combat and you really feel like a hero pulling off some spectacular moves, even in car combat you can shoot wheels off or fuel tanks for spectacular explosions.

Great game, recommended!

«Добро пожаловать в Дубай, джентльмены».
Что же касается деталей сюжета, то тут стоит выделить два аспекта.
Во-первых, неплохих персонажей. Поначалу этого о них и не скажешь, но где-то после середины игры, когда начинается самая жесть, и капитан Уокер, и его подчиненные, и все вокруг начинают не только раскрываться, но и меняться. 1. The marketing materials for this have such a focus on vehicular customization that it had me believing it was going to be Skyrim w/ a ♥♥♥♥♥en hot rod. Really, it is an action game set in an open world sandbox--which is fine too, I guess.
2. Honestly--and just to get it out of the way--the main reason this game is worth playing is because tearing down a sandy highway after an enemy vehicle, harpooning the driver and ripping his flailing body from the soon to be wreckage of his car just never gets old.
3. Obviously, this is set in the Mad Max universe, which has some qualities which are advantageous for a game world. Specifically, it is populated by a breed of murderous subhumans that can be beaten to death by the titular protagonist w/o regard to troublesome and tedious thoughts of morality and necessity. You will invade the shelter of six dudes and kill them all so that you can steal a small amount of scrap metal and dog food, which you need to keep yourself going. In the world of Mad Max, you look at the gray vs. gray morality of this situation, shrug you shoulders and shoot these guys' brothers w/ a harpoon when they come after you.
4. As far as doing the actual killing, combat is solid, esp. when you are in your car. Driving has a pretty standard arcade feel to it, along the lines of GTA games or similar. You have a host of weapons you can use while driving--have I mentioned there's a harpoon gun--and when you go to aim, time slows which enables you to both aim and drive reasonably well at the same time. You can also just quickfire at whatever the game guesses you want to shoot, which is often good enough. These sequences seem so cool that I found myself wishing I could go back and replay them in real time just to see what a hardcore badass I am behind the wheel.
5. Combat on foot is mashing one button to attack and occasionally dodging, parrying or hitting another button for a finisher. The combat looks awesome on screen but I found myself dying because I was trying to rush through the boring fights more than I did because they were actually difficult.
6. Every boss fight in Mad Max is dodging the well telegraphed attack and coming back and beat on them for a minute. Sometimes they throw enemy mobs at you as a distraction.
7. The setup for the story here is Mad Max shows up in a particular section of wasteland, well on his way to reaching some probably imaginary paradise, and he is in search of gasoline. This dude, Scrotus, who has a very bad temper due to being picked on because of his name, runs this little section of wasteland takes issue w/ Max. An altercation ensues leaving Scrotus almost dead and Max w/o his beloved automobile. They become mortal enemies at this point because why not. Max runs into a helpful hunchback named Chumbucket--because people are always named after fishing terms in the endless desert--and together they seek to build Max a new automobile. Along the way, Max runs into the one other person in this vast stretch of desert who is not a degenerate mutant or otherwise horribly decrepit and it just so happens she's an attractive woman who just so happens to have a daughter who just so happens to get kidnapped. *Spoilers* This whole business plays out about how you expect for the most part.
8. The desert setting here is really remarkably good looking. Plains spread endlessly in all directions at the start but you eventually run into plateaus and more mountainous regions which provide a decent diversity of terrain--you know, for a desert. Structures are unfortunately not as diverse. These are all from the same school of architecture used in every post-apocalyptic game world, which is to say they are either half fallen old buildings or randomly thrown together circles of shipping containers, broken down school buses and sheet metal. Either way, the floorplans were made after careful, post-apocalyptic study of Doom 2 WADs and the resulting structures resemble neither functional abodes nor practical defensive works in the least.
9. The various friendly encampments, called strongholds, are inhabited by nameless and long suffering humans who never move anywhere at all. In one, there is a woman vomiting against the wall in a hallway. If you come back at night time, she is still there vomiting in the hallway. After you've helped the stronghold and improved their access the resources, she eventually gets better and thanks you the next time you pass her in the hallway... Just kidding! She will vomit against the wall for all time and nothing you do matters. I presume this is because Mad Max is meant to be allegorical to a real-life existential crisis but maybe the developers, Avalanche Studios, overshot their budget on high-paced harpoon gun action before they got to making realistic NPCs. Who knows for sure.
10. The various characters you run into are all visually alluring and then more or less completely flat. Everyone is either sociopathically self interested or some hot woman who had her daughter kidnapped. It bears pointing out that Max is not in the latter category. The voice acting for these unfortunate folks seems pretty uneven to put it mildly but I really blame the script and the characters themselves over the actors for this.
11. There is a lot to do in Mad Max and the world is pretty expansive. Fast travel isn't enabled until later in the game (and not necessarily at all) and you will spend a good chunk of time just driving from one end of the map to the other, which isn't really a bad thing. Any trip will inevitably be punctuated by a few violent run-ins w/ enemy vehicles and, at least when you are new to an area, diversions to take down enemy defensive structures w/ your handy harpoon gun. This is incredibly fun at first but wears thin as the endless repetitive combat and detours to search for small amounts of resources for upgrades grows tiresome. Most of the sidequesting you do is simply traveling to a particular location, killing everyone and maybe picking up a needed item. It doesn't really add any depth to overall gameplay vs. just randomly driving around and doing whatever strikes your fancy.
12. The customization much lauded by the marketing materials is the main reason you travel around this endless expanse of samey enemy camps and encounters and it's fairly well done. Max himself and many vehicle components are strictly upgrades from previous versions but there are a good deal of choices that improve one stat while harming another. You can build up a tank that can batter its way through large caravans of enemies or put together an agile car to leave them in the dust. Ultimately, some stats become obviously more important than others and I have a feeling most players w/ similar resources collected will end up w/ similar vehicles. In some places, the game  actually forces you to build a particular car and use it, which I feel is basically an admission by the developers that some builds are worthless and you'd never use them if left to your druthers.
13. Despite how my previous twelve points have read, I can honestly whole-heartedly recommend Mad Max to anyone who wants a fun and bombastic game to screw around w/ for a dozen or so hours. I said car combat is awesome and I'm not kidding. Check it out. My advice for the best experience is just resolve to build up a car, whoop some♥♥♥♥♥and put the game down when that gets boring. Finishing out story mode ultimately proves unsatisfying and is deeply frustrating due to a few racing sections toward the end that diverge from core gameplay enough that they just feel tacked on. This is a 100% completionist's nightmare but a weekend (road) warrior can sure have a good time.

If you buy this game, you may just be serving a sentence of your own...as time slips by, engroused in what you are doing. It's a fantastic managment, builder where the unpredictability of the prisoners (and pretty much everything else!) always has you interested.
The Pros:
- Just one more thing: Oh how mnay times I've thought "I'll just finish this bit and then I'll quit...no, wait, I'll do this bit too before I forget....oh and..."
- Organised Chaos: Prisoners are fun to watch, can be easy or difficult to manage. I've built only 3 or four prisons (early access) and have had everything from zero problems almost at all, to a riot that started literally 3 seconds after I accidently overpowered my electricity generator (leaving one gaurd dead and many prisoners bloody and unconscious!).
- Loads of space to build
- lots of info and lots to do. There's always plenty to do and work on.
- It's just damn fun and a good amouont of challenge
Take or leaves:
- Graphics: I like them, you should not be out off by them. There is a 3D mode, but it dodn't do much for me and I prefer the original personally
- Prisoner mode: you can be one of the prisoners and try to escape your own or anyone else's who have shared it in the Steam workshop. It was ok when I tried it but no real sense of actually living in the prison from what I tried. A hit and giggle feature but maybe I need to check it out again.
Cons:
- The tutorial and general information on how to actually play and whatthings do is very much NOT clear. I played the campaign tutorial a few times after extended breaks away from the game when it was in early access and I have avoided it this time around since its official release, so it may have been improved. But overall, you will almost certainly need to look up wikis and how to's, often for very simple thing. Thankfully, there is loads of community help and a working answer is easily found.
- Randomness that could be bugs or just lack of info: Sometimes you don't know why things are not working. Sometimes there are unclear clues, other times you 'll be cratching your heads (I have a few armed gaurds and security gaurds that gather together every night in the yard for no apparent reason. They are not scheduled to patrol there, but they do it anyway).
Really though, I find when I have a go at this game, I am sucked in for many long running sessions. Enough depth to satisfy a passionate builder/manager, not too much as to overwhelm. Eg, there are things like circuits and pressure plates, but you most definitely don't NEED them to run a prison (but it would help of course).
Very much recommended.

I really wanted to like this.  It has nice art and atmosphere, but it's just not fun.
The game basically feels like a tedious process of desperately trying to find what you need to click on, followed by all-too-brief moments of actual puzzles.
The "quests" are started by clicking on something in the environment (indicated on mouse-over), followed by collecting a bunch of needed pieces to activate the associated puzzle.  The pieces in the environment are not uniform in size or appearance, and there is no visual indication to differentiate a clickable piece from a static piece of the background.  The pieces are often very small, and frequently seem deliberately designed to blend into the background or feel like an unremovable part of another object.  When coupled with the fact that there is no visual indication, and some things that look like the pieces *aren't*, it becomes more frustrating than fun to find these pieces.
There is a help system, which involves collecting mosquitoes to "charge up" for use.  You do this by (surprise?) clicking the mosquitoes.  The help seemed almost useless, with nothing happening often times when clicked - as if you weren't on the right screen for the help to assist, nothing would happen.  I also clicked it once and then clicked an item, resulting in the collected "charge" being lost, with no help given...commence more mindless clicking.
The level design also frequently means that if you haven't started a "quest", you can't get the associated items even if you are staring right at them, meaning once you are able to get the quest you have to go back through all the screens you had already visited collecting the items you'd seen but couldn't previously get.
My final gripe is with the actual puzzles where you had to solve jigsaws / place items in their correct spots.  It was incredibly picky about the pieces being aligned near perfectly, and - in at least one of the puzzles - the pieces would fly back to their original location if not placed properly.  In one of these puzzles, pieces also seemed deliberately hidden in the environment.
Basically, this game is less about solving proper puzzles and more about testing your vision looking for tiny, obscured, clickable things.
Amazing, I thought I'd dislike this, but it's so fun, especially when you're killing time.

I first heard of the 'Borderlands' series when I watched an episode of Game Theory about Handsome Jack (FYI go watch that it's great), and it seemed like fun to me. Eventually, the game was on sale and I gave it a try... Holy cow it didn't disappoint! Although I personally haven't played it with friends, I noticed many places where co-op would be great. For example: having to go through the Raid on Digistruct Peak by yourself multiple times might get boring (should you not like making people explode), but with a friend or two it becomes more challenging, which could make it more fun to play, and more bearable to play through more than once.
Some games get criticised for their DLC's. Sure, Borderlands 2 has very many, but most of them are character skins and outfits. The playable DLC's, however, are a blast. The wacky yet immersive story of Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon's Keep and the challenges of Mister Torgue's Campaign of Carnage were the most fun for me personally. You might think otherwise, but these are the ones I'd recommend.
No game is perfect, and this one is no different. If you try to defeat a Raid Boss on your own, you have to be quite overleveled (I was lvl 39 when taking on the lvl 32 Hyperius the Invincible, and still had trouble). However, this might also be because I'm just not that great at the game ;). The timed missions are impossible for me to beat (might also be because I'm bad).
All in all, I would most certainly recommend this game. It's a fun experience for you on your own or with some friends. Giant bosses, memorable characters, fun storyline, epic DLC, cool soundtrack... and Handsome Jack.

Okay. Here goes.
I may have played this game for 2 hours in all, butthat was because my computer crapped out on me and i had to put it in the shop.
AFter two weeks, it came back to me, completely wiped to factory specs because of a nasty virus.
Two hours of gameplay, however, is enough to me to recommend this game.
The character customization itself is enough to keep me occupied for 45 minutes or so, as there are a large number of races that include the "average" fantasy races like dwarves, wood elves, dark elves, and even two different kinds of fae (we'll get into that in a moment), but there are also unique and interesting creatures like the Frogloks (good aligned frog people), Ratonga (Rat folk the size of dwarves) and two different species of lizardfolk.
Also, this game gives you the option between good and evil. there are a surprising amount of evil aligned classes (and good, too, for you light siders out there) and the choice of alignment changes starting areas and such.
The deity you decide to worship (much like neverwinter) will give you buffs and items. UNLIKE neverwinter, the deity you worship actually matters in the game. Depending on the amount of of worshippers, the god or goddess can materiallize in the world as an Avatar, giving server wide buffs to worshippers and offering quests.
And if you're like me, you will want to spend thousands of hours playing this game purely because of collectables. Artifacts and books (much like Rift) are scattered everywhere, and they seem much more common in this game than in Rift. I can't really walk 40 feet ithout finding something interesting, whether that's an artifact, wierd enemy, or absolutely beautiful view.
This game is VERY pretty, in my opinion. I have it on lowest settings because of preference (I want performance, not quality) but I've seen some things in my TWO whole hours that make me think "Wow."
The good starter area, for instance, is on an icy continent/island/archipelago thing, and the ocean is VERY deep. I was a froglok, so i could breathe underwater, and i stopped before finding the bottom because i kind of wanted to play instead of swim downward for a lifetime.
Definately give it a try, better than WOW in my opinion, mostly because they don't try as hard to suck every penny out of you.
Yes, there is a cash shop, but you can definitely play without spending a dime. I know, i looked around in it.

I don’t quite understand why this game receives mixed reviews here, with only 64 % positive. I agree that always-online DRM is a questionable business practice and may be criticized, but it gave me no trouble, I was always connected promptly and stably. And apart of that, everything about this game is great.
+ Runs well and looks nicely on low-spec rig (AMD A10 + GTX 750 Ti).
+ Superb stealth mechanics and fun system of disguises. It’s in fact adventure game with solving environmental puzzles and looking for secret ways. I’ve only murdered my target with a gun once, and that was because of mere laziness.
+ Vast levels full of content that you can use for unseen access or as traps. Also, every level introduces some original mechanics (like doors opened according to your clothing in Hokkaido).
+ Challenges, contracts, achievements, unlockable starting locations, smuggled items et cetera to boost replayability. It’s really awesome to have 20+ ways to get rid of a single target. You can use the list of challenges as an inspiration, or you can try figure everything out yourself.
+ Highly customizable HUD/UI and an option to save manually to adjust difficulty (no more painful checkpoint system like in Absolution, thank god) – manual saving lets you experiment more.
+ The playtime was about 16 hours on my first run, but I’ll definitely replay the whole story in order to try new approaches + look at the bonus content (escalations and elusive targets, which are BTW a great way to keep the game alive and make players return).

This game is a very good game. With its problems of course, but still all in all a good game.
First up, Cons:
-The fact that you need an internet connection to obtain any challenges (Not a problem if you have good internet)
-Occassionally guards can see through walls (IO Interactive have been doing their best to patch these out)
-A very generic, predictable story (The game truly shines when it comes to gameplay, however)
Now to the good stuff
Pros:
-The episodic format. With much more time to develop their game, IO Interactive put out a much better product than they would've with a delayed, full release
-Hitman roots. This game borrows the best of Blood Money (level design, freedom) and the best of Absolution (shooting, the Focus system, graphics) and throws in references to both
-The scale. Evey level is big and open (one is an entire seaside Italian town) and they are filled with interesting NPCs. If you want or if you get bored, you'll find yourself paying attention to the entire backstory of just a passing tourist rather than the already interesting main targets
-Opportunities. The game has events called opportunities that will direct you through an assassination. Don't worry, if that isn't your thing you can totally ignore these, although the scripting and fun is one of the best parts of the game
-Challenges. I'd say that one of the biggest flaws of the older Hitman games is that there were lots of exciting assassinations the game would never tell you about. Thats been fixed by the addition of challenges, some of which can be accomplished through opportunities and others you will be told nothing about. And each one for literally every level is always enjoyable. They are tense, fun, frustrating, hilarious, but above all else satisfying
-Reward System. Each level has its mastery level which can be accomplished by completing challenges. As you go up the ladder, you unlock better gear, tools, weaponry and starting locations. At level 20, the cap, you will gain the best rewards, and while the rewards that precede them are not always useful, these are always good
-Starting Locations. An entirely new addition to the HItman franchise, starting locations are unlocked via mastery leveling and give you a disguise. For example, at level 4 (I believe) in Paris, you can start in the kitchen as a waiter, making assassinations much more easier. These add so much freedom combined with the gear you collect, and if you like speedrunning, these open the door to some very interesting ones indeed
The best thing about this game was that I actually started off with a very negative opinion of this game. After I bought it, I ran into a game breaking bug. A month later, it was patched out and I could resume playing. I almost decided to see if it was still eligible for a refund, but I decided to give this gem another shot. And I fell in love with it. If I can fall in love with this brilliant game after such a messy start, I am sure you can too.
Like good and old Hitman games.

A game that started as a buggy, content-lacking mess, is now one of the most underrated games of the year.
Right now it consists of tutorial and 6 actual episodes, but don't let that small number fool you. Each map is HUGE, and filled with different ways to kill, subdue and hide your targets(and random npc's if you ♥♥♥♥ up).
Challenges are plentiful on each map, and doing them unlocks new gear, weapons and starting locations/disguises.
Story and lore are on point here. Of course, it's not Witcher or Bioshock levels of great story, but compared to other games in series, it is really good. Many dialogues between NPC are pretty fun, and can give you valuable info about target's backstory and potential way to eliminate them.
Performance has been fixed, game no longer stutters every time you enter a big crowd as it did on release.
Live content is pretty fun. Contract cretor/search are easy to use now, and give you lots of ways to restrict the way of elimination. Escalation contracts made by devs can be frustrating to complete, but some of them are really worth it. But the best part is Elusive Targets, which are avialible only for a limited time, and if you fail the mission, they are gone. Yes, that sounds limiting and not so fun, but that actually requires you to be more cautious when doing them, especially if you try to go for Silent Assassin ranking with them. They also unlock alternate suits for you to use, which don't change gameplay(apart from some npc dialogue), but they look great and give a little breath of fresh air.
Overall, I'd give this game a 8/10. It is not perfect(though I hope it will get closer to perfection in season 2), but it's still a game worth purchasing and playing, especially if you're a fan of Hitman series.

Despite it being a very good game - Really enjoyed playing it! I have given this review a thumbs down as a flag, as I have included a useful fix for a common launch issue in the game and want anyone experiencing that issue to see this review.
For a while this game ceased to work on my system and many others in the forums shared the same problem, that being that the game freezes in the initial launch phase. Despite knowing it was pretty much a broken game, I decided to try it one last time and as usual the game froze on the black screen. I pressed JUST 'Ctrl + Alt' and was about to hit 'Del' to quit out of the game when the San Andreas credits screen appeared. This had not happened since the game used to originally work fine and would not have happened if I had just loaded the game up and left it for a few minutes to boot up, as before I had left it for about 20 minutes without pressing anything and the game had not progressed any further than the frozen black screen.
Anyway, after I had pressed JUST 'Ctrl + Alt' and saw the credits screen, the game then progressed to the menu screen and I was able to play as normal, with the exception of the main video automatically being skipped where you hear the San Andreas theme and see a few art work shots of a typical in game scene (e.g. a 'drive by and shoot', random in-game characters, etc.), but this really didn't matter to me as I was happy just to have the rest of the game working.
So, if this problem happens to you, launch the game and about 5-10 seconds afterwards press JUST 'Ctrl + Alt', but NOT 'Del' and the San Andreas credits screen should be displayed and then the game should continue to work as usual, of course just without the main video - 'Who cares?'.
Hope this helps anyone with the same issue and happy gaming!

This is probably one of the most underappreciated open world RPGs on the Steam store. It isn't a perfect game by any means, but if you're into cars, the Mad Max movies and Aussie accents, you'll definitely be able to recognise what it does well and have an awesome time. It's sort of like Just Cause 2 meets Tomb Raider meets Red Dead Redemption. Definitely worth the price tag whenever it is on special. No multiplayer.
I had Mad Max on my wishlist for a while, I'd always been a fan of the movies, however, knowing what movie games are usually like (rushed, lacking content, little story), I knew I would never pay full price for this game. Eventually it came on sale for a meagre $6 which was a price I couldn't pass up, and boy, was I pleasantly surprised (maybe
is a better word) at the game I received.
The game opens with a pretty standard sort of cinematic cut scene, nothing unexpected here, max loses his car to some marauders and basically ends up thrown in a ditch. At this point, you take control of Max. You'll notice that, strangely enough... it seems as if the game actually looks graphically better than the cut scene before it... you guide him through to an open area where you overlook the wasteland and at this point, being a bit of a graphics wh*re, I stopped in my tracks and just panned the camera for a few minutes - This is something that you will do often in Mad Max. This game is graphically... absolutely stunning. The wasteland is dusty and desolate with fragments of the old world dispersed throughout. The heat distortion and detail on the cars is truly something to behold and that's before I get to the
which are some of the best I have ever seen in a game. I'd say the beauty in this game is probably what allowed me to play it for such a long time after the main story was over.
You soon meet your mechanic, Chum, who rather religiously tends to your main car in the game, his
. The Opus is fully customisable and there are a plethora of performance mods and weapons to unlock here using the in-game currency, scrap - which can be conveniently be found just about everywhere. There are other cars in the game however none of them allow Chum to ride along and you will quickly realise that his repair skill and manning of an air-propelled harpoon gun are somewhat invaluable. I was not a fan of this because it really does deter you from using the other cars in the game, of which there are quite a few. I'd also like to mention that fuel conservation is basically not a thing, fuel and water are commodities which you will almost never run short of and I don't feel this is appropriate considering the apparent shortages in the lore and movies. Nevertheless, the car combat is another strong point in this game, it is well thought out and relatively consistent. Very enjoyable despite the somewhat average driving physics. I'm a car guy and the physics didn't put me off but this is by no means a driving sim, far from it.

You will spend the majority of your time clearing out camps of Warboys and establishing stability in the four main regions. The combat on foot is mostly melee oriented, the only guns in this game are your shotgun (which you will not use much) and a handful of snipers (which aren't much of an issue once you figure out that Chum's harpoon gun can pluck them from their nests with ease). The hand to hand combat is very intense and absolutely brutal. It's very satisfying despite its repetitive nature. The enemies unfortunately are not very varied and if you go through the game expecting combat to change you will be disappointed. Eventually you will come to the conclusion that it is easier to just drive around camps spamming (you guessed it) Chum's harpoon gun, which is a one hit kill for all enemies. Later in the game it even gets a grenade attachment which when fully upgraded, one-hits any vehicle you will encounter as well. As a result, combat in this game both on-foot and in-car is as difficult as you want it to be. You could just not use the harpoon and then it would be quite challenging however it is just so fast and easy to use the harpoon that the temptation is real.
I suppose it's time for me to get to the story and characters... this is... not this game's strong point. I can remember maybe... three of the characters in this game? They are all so weak and despite decent Aussie voice acting you will find yourself glossing over most of what they say. You don't really care about any of the characters because they are never developed so when they kill off a few it's a bit like... eh whatever... The story is linear and pretty simple. You help out a settlement, they help you get to the next place, you help them out, they help you get to the next place, some stuff happens, the game ends. Preston Garvey would be proud but it has very little replay ability that's for sure. If this game had multiplayer, it would be very much like Red Dead Redemption. There isn't multiplayer though and I don't really think it would work too well anyway because of the way combat in it is structured.
To end on a good note, the map is colossal and intelligently designed. You really get a sense of scale when you're driving through it. It is a masterfully created wasteland and because of the vehicular aspect, it is appropriately massive unlike in the Fallout universe. Fragments of the old world,
litter it and there is always another location to check out, clear out, and loot. It would be boring driving the considerable distances from place to place if not for the random Warboy encounters and beautiful visuals. Every single camp, big or small is uniquely designed which makes it interesting to investigate the sometimes extremely creative (and sometimes grotesque) designs. There are not a whole lot of different things to do in the world however you'll always be in a different place with a different feel while doing them.
Visuals - 10/10 - Absurd attention to detail, beautiful explosions and world-building.
Sound - 7/10 - Decent sound, a few bugs, nothing special.
Optimisation - 8/10 - Runs really well, GTX 660 has no issues with "Very High" @1080p. Large 32GB file size.
Action - 8/10 - Intense and gritty punch-ups, masterful car combat. Repetitive.
Characters - 2/10 - Weak and barely memorable characters. Max's comments are as numerous as they are grim.
Story - 2/10 - Simple and uninteresting no-choices story line. Very little replay-ability.
Overall a game for a certain kind of person, although I think when it goes on sale for $6 anyone could justify this purchase.
Update 25/11/2017 - This game is still great :)

This game is, by far, one of my favorites. I've been playing this game for a few years (though my Steam account would say otherwise xD) and have come to love this game very much in doing so. It is a very large game, with tons of other players. You get a set list of servers to play on, and you do get a limit to how many characters you can have on your account.
Character creation&Basic Character Stuff:
There is a vast horizon of options to choose from for your character's appearance. I have always found anything besides character height, race, and head/face options a bit unnecessary, since most of the time your armor (appearance and/or actual equipment) will cover it. But, it's still fun to give your character that tattoo that nobody will see, right? ;)
Names are also an interesting thing in this game, because once you reach a certain level, you can give your character a last name. I can't list too many games off the top of my head that will let you give your character a last name. There are also two different equipment tabs. One of them is the equpiment that you wear for the item bonuses such as stat boosters and whatnot. If you don't have any appearance equipment, the other equipment tab, then this is the gear you'll see. Appearance equipment is also another interesting aspect of this game; tons of players with different combinations of equipment in their appearance slots mean it's hard to find two players that look the same.
Mounts are another wonderful aspect of this game. With tons of different mounts, there really is almost no limit to going places.
Gameplay:
The gameplay of this game is rather simple, in all reality. You get a ton of spells that you use, and the amount increases with progression through the game, and go into hotbars. A majority of combat in this game is, in most cases, just clicking of the icons in your hotbar. The animations for your spells aren't too impressive in themselves, unless your graphics are cranked up, however, don't let this deter you.
The story for each character class is fairly different, being that in the end, each character begins on a story to get their epic weapon, the weapon for each class that will become their signature (though often, becomes replaced in-game due to stats not being impressive enough) weapon of choice. Each expansion adds to the story, too, that goes beyond your epic weapon. Even if you aren't paying attention to the stories you get into in too great detail, this game is just fun to play.

At launch the game had horrendous optimisation in areas of the map, even on high end PCs. They've patched this recently with the new rendering engine.. however there are a few problems that still exist:
Cons:
- * While in the drivers seat the cabin is unoptimised when you have the dash light or head lights turned on which results in a FPS loss(10-15 FPS on my rig).
-*Lights are still unoptimised.
-* On GNU/Linux systems with multi-monitor setups, the game ALWAYS uses the monitor furthest to the left. It's irritating. In my setup I have a 1440x900 on the left, 1440x900 on the right, and a 1920x1200 in the middle. The game will not see any resolution > 1440x900 despite the middle one being primary, and it refuses to enter fullscreen on any monitor except the one furthest to the left.
- * While turning corners sometimes your trailer gets stuck even when the tire just is scraping on the curb.
- * Trucks and Buses on single lane roads go half the speed limit(not really a con, but kind of annoying)

This is a nice little point&click/picture hunt/jigsaw puzzle game, with little animated cut scenes. In general, you explore each screen clicking on machines, which give you items to hunt for. Once you find the items you drag the items back to the machine, which might open a new area up, open a door, reveal a puzzle to solve, or finish the level. The puzzles are quite varied but I only found one to be difficult (the steam pipes - it took me a while to figure out what was wanted here). On each level there are also a certain number of puzzle pieces to find. When you complete a level, you can assemble the pieces into a jigsaw puzzle. The game took me a few hours to complete, and I enjoyed the puzzles, but I was a bit sad to see it end so quickly.  When you complete the game you go to a special level that allows you to replay the puzzles. One side note - I did manage to complete one level without finding one of the puzzle pieces, but the finished jigsaw had all the pieces in place at game's end - was that intended? I recommend this game for under $10.

Trusting only the reviews, I bought this game on a whim without much knowledge of what the game was. It is one of those games so darling in its inventions that you'll have to check it yourself to understand the fuss. The art style reminds me of original Pixar sketches and are aesthetically flushed in simple pastels and coloured in complementary contrast tints of green, blue, orange, brown and grey.
Unlike the storyline offered in the description, it didn't seem as if I was saving a planet as everything seemed hunky-dory despite the meteor hit. Instead, as I
still fixing odd broken gadgets here and there, it felt as if I were the new mechanic on Tiny Planet and through my work, the tales of its inhabitants were shown to me in a fabular form. These are tales of life and happy souls which will lighten your spirits from all megrims and entertain with a puzzle variety ranging easy to medium which are all jolly good fun. It has been the most enjoyable hidden object game I've played on Steam as through the course of most of this game you will be searching for a variety of items to fix things and open up new paths and stories.
Other than hidden object puzzles and jigsaws, the puzzles consist of sequential move puzzles using 2D sliding puzzles as well as tiling puzzles, construction puzzles, 8-bit games, memory games and code breaking puzzles. Keeping in mind that is entertaining and soothing for adults, it hasn't any word games and lacks any true challenge that would be too different to progress through for children. It has the medium difficulty crucial for enjoyment from wider audiences so you'll definitely spend time figuring things out but none will take more than a few minutes for mature or experienced puzzlers.
The Steam Library has a Music menu which seemed pointless to a person who'd never really come across any fantastic gaming soundtracks which felt like proper music and not just good game "BGM". I'm not good at writing reviews, so I'll keep it short:
A game with lovable / relatable characters, powerful message(s) and good replayability, despite being a linear story-driven game. Your choices matter. It has a lot of meta-jokes, ridiculous humor and puns (if that isn't your thing, maybe reconsider). The game kept me interested through the whole gameplay.
I say it's well worth the money for such a unique experience.

If you're reading this, it's probably because you are where I was just a few days ago. You spotted Undertale at a tempting price, and despite the rather notorious reputation this games community has, you're wondering if there might be something of value underneath all that hype.
In a word, yes.
Let me start of by prefacing that I am not an RPG guy. I have never played a Final Fantasy game. I don't have a gaming history full of the gems everyone else seems to love of this genre. So understand that when I say that this is a great RPG, I'm not saying that simply because of nostalgia.
The gameplay is, to my knowledge, utterly unique. It seemlessly combines the strategic planning emblematic of the genre with interesting and varied bullet-hell minigames that keep the combat engaging. On top of that, it manages to make itself a meaty challenge without being punishing, a mistake all too common to self-proclaimed "hard" games. It doesn't have the enormous complexity of a more traditional RPG, instead it focuses on nailing a very simple system and letting the depth come from the number of ways it is implemented over the course of the game.
The graphics, while incredibly primitive, do a fantastic job of setting the scene in a simplistic way without relying on nostalgia to be passable. In fact, in many areas they even manage to be rather beautiful.
The soundtrack is amazing, even more so that it was all done by one guy, who also did most of the work on the rest of the game. This is easily up there the best soundtracks of all time, and every song fits the scene perfectly.
The game is short, but honestly I wouldn't prefer it being longer. It never overstays its welcome, or become a grind. It executes everything it sets out to do quickly and effectively, and knows when to move on or end.
Honestly, and this is a rarity for me, I cannot think of many critcisms for this game. The item shops are rarer than I'd like, and the backtracking can be a nusiance when doing the pacifist route, but those complaints are so utterly inconsequential compared to what this game does right.
Now, to get into the rest of what this game does well, I'm going to have to spoil things, which is something I don't take lightly in a game with as good of a story as this. I worry even the light spoilers I intend to get into here might weaken the experience of playing this game through for the first time. So, please, if you are at all convinced by the first part of this review, stop reading this and buy it. If not, hopefully this might convince you without spoiling your experience.
The tone is utterly unique, somehow managing to be a lighthearted parody while still retaining emotional weight. The characters are, despite their cartoonish portrayal, legitimately charming and likeable, while still providing a great deal of humor as the game progresses.
I really feel the need to emphasise the emotional weight portion of that last bit, because that was out of the blue for me on this game. From an outside perspective, especially with the reputation this community has gained, you'd expect this to be an utterly irreverant experience, relying on "LOL SO RANDOM" and meme humor to carry the experience. And while there is some of that in here, it is by far the minority. It is an incredibly effective parody of the genre and video games as a whole, and yet still provides the player with actually difficult and thought provoking decisions as the game goes on.
This is not just a well written game. This may actually be one of the best written games I've ever played. It's to the point where I actually can't write about how great this writing is without spoiling it, which undermines the entire point of this review. So much of my joy from this game was in having my preconceptions about this game utterly surpassed in ways I never expected it to. Much like Spec Ops: The Line, I expect knowing there is a twist coming really spoils the entire game.
So please, if there is even a spark of interest, you owe it to yourself to try it out. Go in knowing as little as possible, and don't let the community scare you away for it. Like all zealots, they are completely divorced from everything that actually makes this game great. Just ignore them and see this game for what it truely is.
It's like what if Yoko Taro created a 8-bit RPG.
