With that said, and me having gone deep into EQ2 I thought it time to write a proper review of MY take on the game good, bad, and the so so.
I found that the game still holds up well with the graphics and the music and zone immersion that can be tricky for any mmo or guge single player rpg to capture correctly.  The game has done a much better job recently of helping showing in the starting zones what skills and combat and crafting and gathering types of game play that is in and wanted by any fan of the mmo game.
The amount of races and classes in this game are incrediable.  Over 25 classes (only 1 or 2 need to be baught in the in game cash shop) and 21 races (2 of which are again in the cash shop that need to be baught to be available).  An let's address that quickly.  Yes some of the best things are in the cash shop, 2 races and 2 classes, and the best housing (no monly in game cost of gold or solver aka "rent") and some other conveinces things like armor skins and very cool mounts.  HOWEVER, free to play players can have a fun, very vast, open world of experience that can easily be over 100 to 200 hours of content if the player wants to simply level to cap and see 10 years worth of zones, dungeons, quests and raids.  Now I went sub, ( I choose to pay monthly to play) as free to play players can not use some chat options and some other limiations I did not want.  However, again I stress a free to play player can come in treat this game (dungeons and raids aside) like Skyrim and have over 150 to 200 hours of free content to see and experience.
An while the style of game is dated after 10 years and the combat again very classic Everquest or World of Warcraft, for some of us that is a plus and not a minus.  I do want to stress this point out for modern mmo fans that if you are looking for a world less static and more "alive" like Guild Wars2 or Rift, or anything else coming our recently this may not be the mmo for you.
For people wanting to play alone, you have (in my eyes) some of the best voice acting that still holds up on most quest s, (75% voice acted), great great immersive zones and music, and a very strong personal and world story to experience.  You can hire mercenaries to aid you in your quest or dungeons, and can always over level a dungeon and do it later to both see it and solo.  Since this game has been out 10 years there are hundreds of zones, dungeons, areas, lands, public (non instance) dungeon zones and private (instance) dungeons to experience.
The only bad or dissapointing aspects of the game to me, other then the game being 10 years old at this point is the dated UI (there are add ons to fix) and the quest mapping and tracking can take awhile to get into and understamd.  Definately advise you find a good community, active player base since I think (I do not know for sure) their are only several hundred thousand to a million players off an on.  However, no zone felt empty and i saw people in every zone and most eager to help or talk to new players.
Overall, while this was not Everquest to me, it is a game i look forward to spending a year or two in off and on to see everything i missed, and to enjoy the next chapter of the Everquest saga before the next chapter in Everquest starts.  To any fan of old school mmo's or single players wanting a vast world to explore you could do far far worse then spend some time in this vast wonderful world.

Right now, think of the "BEST" war movies that you can, just off the top of your head.
You probably got "Apocalypse Now", "Saving Private Ryan", "Full Metal Jacket", maybe even "Come and See".
It's weird that all the "fingerquotes" GOOD war movies are decisively anti-war (which, really, any realistic portrayal of the horrors of war will be seen as "anti-war", it's our natural human reaction) - and yet, all of the "fingerquotes" GOOD war video games are Michael Bay-level masturbatory murder-fests that run in the completely opposite direction...
Spec Ops: The Line is the kind of game I've been waiting for, for a long time.  It is a "GOOD" war game in the sense that "Apocalypse Now" and "Saving Private Ryan" are good war movies.  It uses the video game medium to convey the horrors of war and a soldier's descent into madness in a way no movie ever could.  Admittedly, it's not the best gameplay you'll ever see...
And yet this game has challenged every preconception I had about war crimes, and has completely changed my understanding of the difference between "what is right" and "what is necessary".

Solitaire: LOTR Edition!
This solitaire game is great.  The graphics remind me of Lord of the Rings and other medieval fantasy stories.  The gameplay is solid, a good balance beteween not too many cards and not enough to win.  I've played a lot of solitaire games and this ranks up there at the top in my book.
A unique feature in this game is a bonus when you choose cards of matching suits.  The bonus applies to your companions' power ups.  This adds to the strategy because instead of just choosing cards by number you have to decide if you want to match this one to get the suit bonus or match this other one to clear a column.
You start with one companion, and you get to choose between two different ones.  Along the way other companions will join you  on your journey.  You will have four companions max, one for each card suit.  Some companions are only with you for a little while as they guide you through the terrain, then leave and another companion takes their place.   The companion powers are things like remove a random card, reveal some face-down cards, give you a card that will help match something, etc.
The gold you get during the game can be used to purchase helpful items.  A sword to clcear away vines; An Axe to chop ice; A Mace to break stone.  Those weapons can only be used 3 times in a row before they break.  So you will be buying more from the store every so often.  There is also a key that locks a stack of cards and you can either buy one from the store or hope you find the hidden one beneath another stack of cards.  Occasionally dragonfire will ignite a card for a few turns.   You can purchase a water potion to douse the flames or just wait for them to go away after several card matches.  In addition to those regular use items there are one-time helpful items that are expensive but worth saving up for, such as the one that gives you an extra undo, or one that reveals more face-down cards.
The story is narrated by a man, and I think he does a very nice job.  There is a story page in the beginning of each section of the journey.  There are 10 levels of card play in each section.   This game is strictly solitaire card, no hidden object levels or anything like that.
There are 3 difficulty levels:  easy, normal, and hard.  I played on normal.
This game is very long, so you definitely get a lot of content for your money. 15 +/- hours for the main story on normal difficulty.  And once you beat the main game you can replay levels or play 3 mini-games including the tri-towers layout, or random layout.

It's a little unbalanced at times, but it's a lot more fun than I expected.  It's still Solitaire - not too much of the formula is changed - but it has some items which you can buy or find, and barriers which require specific items, and objectives you have to meet at each level.  It's surprisingly good.

To completely finish story and everything game has to offer, you may reach up to 50 hours or longer. Cinematics are very enjoyable. Story has surprising events, twists & dramatic ending. You also have big ammount of side missions which often reward with car upgrades.
Gameplay off story is pretty much reducing threat level in regions - you do that by destroying camps, removing snipers & towers in the region, fighting convoys or do a race. Off mission rewards is mostly scrap, which you use to upgrade max & your car. To fully upgrade everything you will need to collect 25000+ scrap which is very long process. Getting all this scrap comes with exploration where you often find not only project parts (which you can use to upgrade friendly camps and get some perks) but also stunning sceneries or camp creations.
Mad Max is open world, where you spend most gameplay off missions (unless you rush the game). Slowly upgrading and weaponizing car is necessary to finish late-story missions, but i think you could go through whole campaign with only half the upgrades ive done. Another fun level adds various car weapons, you can get - my favourite is harpoon that you get early in the game to enjoy. While you are not in car, even tho you have shotgun always with you, your main weapon will always be fists. Fighting is decent, i found it especially hard in the beginning, but as i got used to it, i am often able to fight off everyone without getting hit now... Max's skill upgrades adds some extra moves you can perform during fights. Other upgrades improve fist damage, damage resistance or shotgun upgrades...

Don't let anybody tell you that this game isn't god damn great.
Like all good steam reviews i'll start with the things I don't like because if there is one place to get mad, it is on steampowered dot com.
-middling performance (this game nearly maxes out my i5 6600k, my framerate can vary from 100ish to 30ish on a gtx1070). if it's any consolation the performance isn't any better on the consoles lol?
-always online DRM (fwiw I have never noticed Hitman's servers dropping, during my playtime of about one week?? and this was while a sale was going on so i imagine the servers would be under heavier load than usual, but i don't know how their infrastructure works so maybe i'm talking out of my butt. i don't want to excuse DRM or other peoples negative experiences but it just has not affected me personally.)
-overall poor sound work:
This game suffers from the Elder Scrolls problem in that there are about twelve voice actors. Their performances are good! But god, sometimes it feels like every male guard has either one of two voice actors - the guy with the deeper voice and the guy whose voice is just a touch whiny.
moving about one metre so that a wall is in front of an npc will make that npc's dialogue go from clear as a bell to muffled, like you're listening to them speak through an irl closed door.
There are only subtitles for dialogue that alludes to things you can use to murder people and sneak around. Incidental dialogue or the dialogue of characters reacting to the things you do is not subtitled. That's super frustrating, especially for someone like me who loves little bits of dialogue in video games!
Some noises in the game are super loud compared to the rest of the game (for example, I physically flinched when activating the forklift alarm to the left of the entrance to the Colorado level it was so loud). The music can get super loud as well.
- yo the Marrakesh map is kinda lame
Other than that, though, this game is so great. The above are the only things that have bothered me during my time with the game, and even then, they're kind of minor, I feel? I've never enjoyed a hitman game like I have this one.
During my time with Hitman 2016 (22 hours as of writing) those are the only things that have really bugged me? The DRM hasn't affected me personally but I included it because online only DRM isn't acceptable even in 2016. But god, the rest is just fantastic. The levels are beautiful to just wander around in, and watching Hitman's little clockwork worlds go is delightful. The amount of NPCs that IO has fit into those levels is amazing. The movement, aiming and shooting feels good and satisfying, and gunfights aren't hopeless if you're prepared and arent dashing around like a doofus or caught in the open. I haven't completed the story yet, but idk, like... seems decent! 👌
Anyway whatever as someone who very frequently will not purchase a game until it is below ten dollars this is absolutely worth the ~$50NZD I paid for this one. If you're undecided go watch the Giant Bomb quick looks of this game because they're good, even if the guys who're playing don't quite understand everything in the game.

Nearly limitless possibilities for how to stage--and then pull off--assassinations

THE BAD

Super Meat Boy.  The one and only platforming game I've played in the last two years, and it's very easy to explain why. It's good. In fact it's more than good because it's the most excellently executed 2D platformer since Super Mario World. In fact I'm going to say something about that. Everything in this game is a modern take on the retro style of 2D platform games, but as much as it takes from that time long ago, it doesn't completely thrive off of that. It is its own game too.
The gameplay is by far the first and foremost reason why I played this for two years.The controls are incredibly well done, because I never have to worry about something in the game screwing me over (except occasional lag spikes that can't be helped, I blame that it was meant to be on Flash). Every level is treated like a puzzle, and at points, obstacles in a level are treated as a puzzle. It is at times difficult to solve but never unsolvable. And through that you get into the thought process that it will be possible to beat this level as long as I keep trying new strategies. Which makes it addicting as hell, which I love.
The story is simple, but it allows you to fill in the blanks like most games back in the old days. I'm sure they had this in mind the whole time they were making it, and of course it shows through all of the references to older games it makes in easy and not so easy to reach places. The references range from obvious to obscure, but either way you'll at least find a thing or two you recognize.
The music will take you back just like the story does, but it's so well modernized that you wonder to yourself every now and again if you've heard this music before. You haven't, and it gives the game its own originality and atmosphere that you won't find in another game. Danny Baranowsky, the composer for Super Meat Boy is a legend, and this soundtrack will feel like you're going through one or that you are one yourself. That's one impactful soundtrack if you ask me.

I promised myself to never play a COD game and to never fall for it. But one night i was bored, so i started reading about the franchise on Wikipedia. Then i randomly discovers the page on Black Ops 2 and that particular part wich says that this is the only COD game to feature branching storylines, player choices and multiple endings. I just could not say no to that.
Long have i wanted a shooter where i really felt the emotional effect of a soldier's moral choices and consequences, so of course i was very disappointed when Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Patriots was cancelled.
This is in no way an equivalent nor an equivalent of my expectations, but it is the best "moral shooter" out there now that Patriots is gone.
The game has some silly parts and some Americanism/macho cliches that makes me want to vomit but it's survivable.
The game has a firm linear grasp on what's to be considered a failure and victory on some parts, but the gameplay was surprisingly variated unlike what i imagined. I expected all shooters, especially COD, to be ONLY shooting on-foot, reload, shoot more, reload, shoot more and so on. But you get to control air-strikes, drones and robots as well as there be some small different sequences such as driving and flying. Not that much of variation perhaps, but personaly and subjectively, it helped to me.
I hear people mourn about the sci-fi conversion of COD, but i wouldnt want it any other way! If i absolutely have to degrade myself down to the level of playing an FPS, then it sure as hell shall be a sci-fi game, because im a junkie of that and i specialize in that genre as well (game designer). Now thus, i have a question for you guys. I have the feeling that Advanced Warfare is the COD game wich is the most sci-fi heavy title in the series so far and Wikipedia states that critics praised it for having faster tempo than AND more focus on single-player story than previous titles. Now if this is correct im AM going to give that game a try for ♥♥♥♥s sake! :D The question is.....is that true? That AW is like that?
Finally i will end with stating that i still agree with my long-standing opinion on FPS games. They are too repetitive, uncreative, unoriginal and lacks story.......in MY opinion. Have a good one! Oh, and remember to answer the question!

The Tiny Bang Story is point-and-click puzzle game. Gameplay consists of finding hidden objects and solving different puzzles. Every chapter you have to collect different objects and play mini-games. After completing chapter you have to put puzzle parts together to restore planet. All of these go with amazing relaxing music. The playtime was really enjoyable. Sadly it is short in duration.

This is a casual adventure-lite game leaning towards the hidden object genre but without formal "finding scenes". It gets a lot of things right. It has lovely art-work and whimsical world design in the vein of Amanita Designs. It has decent relaxing music. It seems solidly put together and doesn't suffer some of the technical issues of other casual market games of similar vintage with things like alt-tab.
Where it goes a bit wrong is in the mini-game designs. It contains "arcade" mini-games, which many players of these sorts of games are not looking to play. It also has some of the worst examples of colour-blind ignorant puzzle design I've ever seen. It literally has a puzzle where the only "can you work it out?" element is whether you can see colours correctly or not. What makes these choices unforgivable is that the mini-games are unskippable. If you can't complete one then that's it, no more game for you. These are really terrible design choices that will kill the game for many people and that's why I can't recommend it.

Tiny Bang Story is an indie puzzle adventure which drives the player through a beautiful story of family and science.
Good:
Pleasant graphical style. Nice background story told without actual texts. Varying puzzles, some of them worth a redo. Great soundtrack.
Bad:
Puzzles might be too easy or clueless at times. In-game computer games are tedious and uninspired. A little bit short.
Overall, I enjoyed the 3 hours that I spent playing this game. It might be a little bit straightforward, but the good presentation makes your time pleasant while you play TBS.

A third person shooter that defines not only for its superior military shooter experience, but also for its gripping story. The whole game is intense, unique and will certainly stand out from other third person shooters of the like.
You’ll be greeted with a sand-filled Dubai metropolis and a vast desert environment full of dangerous hazards. The lighting, shadows and the small details is what makes this game stand out in the graphics department. It really wants you to see the small details that would usually go unnoticed, nice touch.
It places the player in a situation where a choice must be made whether the player likes it or not. You have come to Dubai for one purpose and one purpose only and that is to locate survivors and radio for Evac. But instead you find this city in the middle of war and the sole purpose of the mission is lost.
Gunshots, the sandstorms and voices sound very clear. There are almost no distortions in the sound that could be heard. Each and every weapon in the game sound different from one another. The character voices sound deep and clear, which is a positive aspect of this game.
The third person shooter style gameplay is just like any other generic third person shooter, it’s nothing special I’ve seen before. But that’s not to say this is a bad game, of course it’s not. It plays out smooth with no significant frame drops from location to location. The controls, the movement speed and the weapon recoil are all very well implemented.
Coming in at a premium price of £19.99, it is on the expensive side when it comes to the ‘pound per hour’ basis. It’ll only take you around 5-8 hours to finish the game, so it only gets a measly 6 for me. You are better off waiting until this game goes on sale for it to be worth buying.

Based upon the classic novella by Joseph Conrad, Spec Ops: The Line deviates from previous entries to tell a harder hitting story. While the gameplay mechanics are stock standard Third Person Shooter, the soundtrack and story help sell a world on fire.
You assume the role of Captain Martin Walker, a man in charge of a small three man squad.  As you enter a devastated Dubai, you realise that your simple reconnaissance mission isn't all that it was cut out to be. You are taken down paths you would normally never take and when you make mistakes, the game lets you know in glorious fashion. That's not to say you can't have fun with this game. Just remember that you shouldn't be surprised if after the first few chapters,♥♥♥♥♥♥hits the fan. This is based on the story that was the basis for Apocalypse Now and if you're going to play this game, you might as well give that a watch.
While the gameplay is fairly simple and standard, TPS, there are a few things that make playing Spec Ops: The Line, a little more interesting. One mechanic is the ability to direct squad mates toward targets. Can't quite get someone yourself? Let your scout/sniper handle it. Want heavy unit control? Let your explosives expert deal with that. As you get bombarded with enemies from every direction, don't forget that your squad mates don't have to help on autopilot. I do have to note that the controls for me were a tad finicky. However, I can simply place that down to my casual gaming status. This other interesting mechanic doesn't affect gameplay as much as the squad control does, but it does help sell the story's descent into madness. As you progress through the game, Captain Walker is placed in increasingly morally difficult positions where one decision now can affect how the game will play later on. Due to the emotional stress you are placed under by your decisions, melee attacks start becoming far more brutal. What used to be a simple elbow to the face, progresses until you end up pummelling a person's face with the butt of your gun before finishing them off with a street justice execution.
All in all, this game is a fantastic experience and certainly challenged me both gameplay wise and morally. I began asking more questions of how simple decisions now can affect how life will be later on. While the decisions you make don't alter the story drastically, whatever choice you make certainly feels like it carries a lot of weight. I guess what I'm trying to say is, this game is a fantastic piece of storytelling, even if the gameplay is your standard TPS. If you are looking for a game that challenges you in more ways than just the gameplay itself, then it is most definitely worth it.

I paid $1USD for this game, and even at that price I still cannot recommed buying it. There are three basic aspects to this game; a jigsaw puzzel, hidden objects, and a number of puzzle games.
Basically, you find hidden objects to unlock various puzzle games which unlock more areas for you to finish collecting the hidden objects you need to pass the level. The various puzzle games aren't bad, and in fact some of them are pretty good; however I still had a number of issues with the game play.
There are two types of hidden objects. Pieces to the jigsaw puzzle that you work on between levels and objects required to unlock the puzzle games or additional areas within a level. Finding the puzzle pieces can present a nice challenge, but the objects related to the mini games are beyond easy to find. The problem with this is that the puzzle peices are completely unnecessary. Whether you find one or all 25, you are given every piece from that level when working on the jigsaw puzzle between rounds. The game doesn't even keep track of how many pieces you have missed nor does missing pieces create gaps in the jigsaw puzzle, which would not only add to the challenge but also give the player some motivation to find all of the puzzle pieces. I also had issues with the jigsaw itself. Basically, every piece of the puzzle was identical in shape and all you had to do was assemble the pieces on top of a to-scale photo of the puzzle. Even the sky/background pieces offered no challenge what-so-ever.
I also found the lack of direction in this game to be a bit of a problem. The description states that there is no text, but there isn't even the tiniest bit of instruction when beginning a mini-game without clicking on the 'hint'. Playing through a second time, I've noticed that some of the hints are simply instructions for the game, while others are actual hints (Which I wanted to avoid using). This was a problem because at the beginning of each game, I found myself clicking around the puzzle a few times in order to see how the controls worked, and on at least two occasions my random clicking actually solved the puzzle before I even had a chance to actually begin. This lack of instruction also meant that the greatest challenge for some puzzles was actually figuring out what you needed to do as opposed to trying to solve the puzzle. Again, there were at least three or four puzzles that were both challenging and fullfilling.
The ending is beyond unfulfilling. After reaching the final screen, there is no "the end", "you won", "congradulations", nothing. You have an oppertunity to replay any of the mini puzzzles that you faced throughout the game, and after collecting enough bugs for a 'hint', the game indicated that I needed to play them. I only did so thinking that this was one final challenge before beating the game. I was wrong.
After beating the mini-puzzles a second time, I started a second game since I had missed a few of the puzzle pieces the first time around. I would have kept looking for them, but if you click on the last object of the level you are forced to move on even if you haven't found all of the puzzle pieces. I was hoping that finding all of the puzzle pieces would earn me some sort of ending. I was wrong. One play through lasts 90-120 minutes which actually makes this the most expensive game playtime/$ of any that I have ever bought on Steam; even after counting the second playthrough etc. I only got 4hours from the game, the rest was just runtime while I was away from the computer.
What really prevents me from recommending this game is the description. Let's talk about the first thing you look at in a game, the price. This game is insanely underpriced for what amount of content it has, not to mention the often sales which make it an even better deal, like right now. For 10€ this game is a bargain, for 5€ it's practically stealing from the devs. This game could have a 30€ price tag and it would be completely justified. So, in that regard, it's great!
This game's graphics are great, they may not be as "good" as the newest COD on ultra (for example), but it's beautiful in it's own regard. This game's graphics are in the style of old SNES games. That means that any old toaster (like mine) can run this game. The music in this game is awesome, every single theme is very well composed, and it fits perfectly. The daytime music is cheerful and upbeat, meanwhile, contrasting that is the night theme which is calm and collected, boss themes are upbeat, etc.
Arguably the most important part of a game. This game is an adventure, survival, sandbox game, however, when I tell you that, that doesn't mean anything, really. This game is an adventure game which lets you beat it whatever way you like, if you wanted, you don't even have to beat every boss to feel completed, you might make a goal that more suits you, like building the biggest and greatest city, maybe you want to collect every single sword in the game, etc. Terraria can be fun and engaging, but only if you make it so. Playing through the game once with a melee character and beating every boss can be fun once, but I personally doubt it will be fun the second time. That's why you need to change it up a bit and make it fun for yourself. There is also a fantastic online multiplayer mode which lets you play with friends, play on public minigame servers, etc.
The insane amount of items, weapons, enemies, bosses is great, however, because of that, the learning curve is very steep. If you aren't willing to go to the Terraria Wiki, or watch some Youtube videos to learn what some items do, or if you want any kind of explanation for anything, then you're gonna get bored and confused after only a little bit of time. Just a warning.
If you ever get bored, you could always download mods. I won't explain mods a lot, you can look up stuff about mods online.
- Get the game. (Or, alternatively, get a 4 pack of the game for the price of 1 copy that's not on sale and give Terraria to yourself and three friends, since it's Christmas)

That's the end of the review, happy holidays everyone!

What are the nine scariest words in the English language? "We're Delta Force and we're here to save you!"
It's been four years since I played Spec Ops: The line. Since then it's lingered in my mind, occasionally taking me back and causing me to relive the horrors. Even now, I'm still not sure what genre to place it in. Action drama or action tragedy perhaps? Whatever genre it's in, I know this:
It's the number one of all time.
In some games, the only way to lose is when you turn the game off and stop playing. Here, it's the only way to win. And I strongly doubt many players have won. Your desire to finish, to see what comes next, is expertly pitted against your better judgement. Almost always the former prevails over the latter.
Of course, there are those harping on mediocre 2007 gameplay or shoehorned in multiplayer. I surmise that they have completely missed the point. It's like criticising a masterwork painting for being in a shoddy museum or having a dirty frame. This is doubly true because Spec Ops' message is about being in such a museum, poking fun at the box it comes in.
Poking fun is entirely the wrong word, so instead let's call it poking nauseated revulsion.
If you have a timemachine, go back to 2012 and tell yourself to play it. If you lack such a device, reading this review alone probably spoils too much. Part of the experience was going into it thinking it was Modern Warfare 2. The real reasons to play it now are academic, archeological. Also the soundtrack is pretty good.
Verdict: Recommended, perhaps above all to see what the hype was about.

Ori and the Blind Forest: DE is arguably the best metroidvania style game i have played in the last 5 years. Comparing against games such as Guacamelee, Shadow Complex, Axiom Verge, Dust and even to some extent Cave Story. This game is absolutley gorgeous, giving an oasis in the woods feel that makes you geniunely happy to play the game and explore new areas. Speaking of areas, i noticed one of the negative reviews touched on the lack of new content delivered in the Definitive Edition of the game, which mind you is correct. Black Root Burrows, with proper knowledge of the area can be traversed in under 10 minutes. However, something about the addition of an area solely focusing on the light and dark aspect of the world, rarely present in the main game, gives this area a totally unique feel and seems to fit perfectly with the original game. Instead of looking at this area as a new addition try and look at the definitive edition as just that, the way the game should be. I could just as easily say it took me 5 minutes to get to wall jump, does that area feel any less interesting or complete. Alright lets move on to the always present pros and cons.
PROS:
- The sound direction. This game has an beautiful and atmospheric soundtrack fit for the area the game takes place in.
- The movement. Oh god the movement. This is the reason i picked up this game as a speedrun and added it to my top ten games of all time. Every motion feels fluid, wall jumps that give that spiral animation are so damn satisfying. Ech ability gained always adds to that movement as well. I never felt like i got an ability and was overpowered in terms of travesing the world. Okay....maybe bash but....bash is super fun and can be used in such creative ways.
- The story. I won't go into it too much but goddamn what a tearjerker. nuff said
- The abilites. Each ability gained feels like a new tool in your aresenal, epanding your movement options to allow for more creative traversal. Not gonna spoil anything but just wait for bash, it will blow your mind.
- The CHEATCODE. okay, so for most this doesnt seem like a big deal and honestly it isnt much of one but if you hit left, up, right, down, up, up, up, jump, Ori will change into one of an infinite amount of colors adding some diversity to a character who is usually stark white. Idk its just cool and it brings me back to the old days of button combos on start screens to get cool effects.
- Sequence Breaking. im not spoiling anything but if you beat the game and are curious, go check out grimelios on youtube, very cool vids detailing sequence breaks and tricks in Ori.
CONS:
- The difficulty. While there are many settings in place to curb the difficulty this game is punishing as hell. If you explore and ge the health cells it will be a breeze but for those who like to rush through games, be careful. Its hard but not bad once you've learned the mechanics. nuff said.
- alright umm... im actually sitting here having a hard time coming up with more cons other than "its hard"
- i guess if i had to give another con, some areas you can progress really far in only to reach the ending and fins out you arent able to pass without a certain item. It happened to me twice but honestly at least you know how to get back there once you've gotten the item.
Sorry i went a little light on the cons, its honestly really hard for me to find something this game doesnt do well. the underwater sections are well paced and can be skipped entirely if you know what you are doing. The flying feels dynamic with the inclusion of the bash and the ending feels satisfying. Definitely give it a try if you are on the fence. Moon Studios has outdone themselves.

It changes the familiar game-play formula drastically while still keeping the creepy vibe of the Five Nights at Freddy's series. It's easy to tell that this game had a bit more budget behind it with more sophisticated visuals and stellar voice acting. The game play is pretty solid and each night introduces unique mechanics, meaning you never really get into a comfort zone as you progress through each night. This leaves you feeling a bit of fear and tension as you progress through the game, well at least up until night 4. Night 4 puts a bit of a damper on the rest of the experience. The infamous night was a long and cumbersome battle, and I got jump-scared so many times that it quickly lost its novelty. This took away from night 5 as well. What should have been a tense exciting finale, felt a bit more derivative because the jump-scares just didn't feel like a threat anymore after all my struggles with the previous night. Night 4 gripes aside I still thoroughly enjoyed the experience, and I feel this game conveys the plot in a more direct and concise manner than any other game in the series. This was definitely a welcome breath of fresh air for the Five Night's at Freddy's series.
Pros:
Solid and unique tense game-play
Visually more advanced and creepy than previous games.
Great voice acting really coveys plot
Cons:
Night 4 was a bit difficult and detracted from overall experience.

Let me explain Hitman to you. In a simple way so it isn't confusing.
Hitman is a game where you are asked to assassinate a target. Sometimes two. Sometimes more. These targets do not want to die, obviously but they do not know they are about to. Your job is to be a literal grim reaper. Death can come in many shapes and sizes and the fun comes in finding out ways to kill your target. One day, it's a shot to the head. The next day, maybe they fall off a cliff. Some days, they suffer death from flesh eating virus or exploding rubber duck. Pretty much all you need to know is that the world is wide open, lots to see and do and it's a pleasure to play after how awful Absolution was.
The whole season is full of things to do. Not just the story mode stuff. Each map also contains escalation missions, which are missions that grow harder each time you do it by adding new targets, rules and stipulations to them. Every so often, a timed exclusive mission will come up too where you can earn some extra outfits for 47. Dressing him like some kind of weird murderous Ken doll (If Barbie is into that thing).
The only downside to the game is its always online connectivity. If you go offline, you lose all your progression and unlocks. This is kinda BS considering it shouldn't need to be online, but i guess it's to stop hackers and what-not. It's not an excuse, I'm just not personally bothered by things like that.
At the time of writing this, it's 50% off due to Black Friday. Get it. For that price, you are getting a chunk of game and Season 2 is due next year!

ESP / ENG
ESP:
Otra entrega de Batman, que aunque no goza de la misma calidad de Arkham City - y Arkham Asylum - dará bastante guerra. Aunque la historia no explica mucho de los orígenes, nos encontraremos ante un Batman antes de conocer a enemigos como Bane o El Joker. Un juego de acción y aventura realmente bien hecho y que también tiene sus buenas horas de juego. Combatiremos contra bastantes enemigos potenciales y nos moveremos de nuevo por la ciudad de Gotham para castigar el crimen. En ésta entrega, Batman contará con nuevos juguetes para combatir y el desplazamiento rápido que nos permitirá ir de un punto a otro con un solo clic. Otra entrega de Batman que no decepciona.
Una vez acabada la campaña, merece la pena jugar el DLC "Cold, Cold Heart" ya que nos dará unas cuantas horas más de diversión. Pero en caso de no poseerlo, también podremos entrar en las partidas multijugador en la que aleatoriamente puedes ser Batman, Robin o los soldados del Joker o de Bane. Conseguir puntos de control y matar al enemigo es un disfrute, sobretodo cuando vas subiendo experiencia y consiguiendo, desde nuevas apariencias, hasta nuevas armas y habilidades.
Pros:
- Buena campaña (aunque no tan buena como las de RockSteady)
- Excelente ambientación, apartado gráfico y sonoro
- Sistema de combate muy bien elaborado y entretenido
- Multijugador (Que no se encuentra en las entregas anteriores)
Contras:
- BUGS: Sin encontrar bugs en las anteriores entregas, en esta hay bastantes bugs, sobretodo gráficos. Por ejemplo, entrar en una habitación y que no haya ni texturas, de hecho, hasta a Batman le faltan texturas
- Gatgets (Batgagets) : Los nuevos juguetes de Batman le llegan a hacer prácticamente invencible y eso es algo que le quita toda la gracia al factor riesgo en combate.
- Historia: No es una mala historia pero flojea mucho. Parece que en cuanto al desarrollo de la trama, no le ecahron la misma dedicación que en las anteriores entregas, pero al fin y al cabo no es de RockSteady.
ENG:
Another installment of Batman, although not enjoying the same quality of Arkham City - Arkham Asylum and - given enough war. Although the story does not explain much of the origins, we find before a Batman before meeting enemies like Bane and The Joker. A game of action and adventure really well done and it also has its good hours of play. We will fight against many potential enemies and we will move again for Gotham City to punish crime. In this delivery, Batman will have new toys to combat and rapid movement will allow us to go from one point to another with a single click. Another installment of Batman that does not disappoint.
Once the campaign worth playing the DLC "Cold, Cold Heart" and it will give us a few more hours of fun. But if you do not own it, we can also get into a multiplayer game in which randomly can be Batman, Robin or soldiers of Joker or Bane. Get control points and kill the enemy is a joy, especially when going up and getting experience, from new looks, to new weapons and abilities.
Pros:
- Good campaign (although not as good as those of RockSteady)
- Excellent atmosphere, graphics and sound
- Combat system very well crafted and entertaining
- Multiplayer (not found in previous releases)
Cons:
- BUGS: No bugs found in previous Batman´s videogames. In this release there are many bugs, especially graphics. For example, entering a room and there are no textures or indeed even Batman missing textures
- Gatgets (Batgagets): The new Batman toys you get to do practically invincible and that is something that takes away all the fun factor to risk in combat.
- History: Not a bad story but weakens much. It seems that in terms of plot development, do not make much work, but after all is not RockSteady.

Oh good lord I finally got around to reviewing this one proper. Woo.
Premise: Super Meat Boy is a terrible platformer.
I don't even know if I'd call it a platformer in fact. It's just... stupid.
Let's list the sins this game commits:
1. Character movement and level design exist in two separate planes; the controls are not tight enough for how precise you're expected to play.
2. Levels all focus on trial-and-error, with no checkpoints anywhere, so levels that go beyond the 15-20 second mark get tedious to replay because you haven't figured out how to complete the last one or two bits of the level. Especially bad in world 6 where all the levels are marathon levels (for this game at least).
3. I hope you like tiny platforms and wall jumps. Also, you slide down walls rather fast, a bit faster than reasonable.
4. Lots of waiting around for the game to allow you to progress. A good platformer should never break the flow of a level for more than a moment; if you have to stand still for over a second to complete a level, redesign the level to be better.
5. The game actively mocks you. Especially if you try to use a keyboard (like I did). But that's because they couldn't be bothered to port it correctly more than anything, since the keyboard controls are quite clunky. Maybe they're partially responsible for my lack of enjoyment, but a PC game should be playable with a PC and nothing else. I've played plenty other difficult platformers on my keyboard but only this one gives me major issues.
6. Grow up, devs. The "humor" is the kind of stuff that only 5-year-olds would find amusing. Minor thing but I don't care at this point.
I can't even lie and say that this game had a chance to be good, because the entire premise of the game is flawed. I can point anyone considering getting this game in the direction of plenty better platformers, if you'd like. Dustforce, FLY'N, Guacamelee, Knytt Underground, Love, Mark of the Ninja, PixelJunk Eden, Rayman Origins and Legends, VVVVVV, heck, even They Bleed Pixels is superior despite being flawed as well. Play any of those, stay away from this abomination.

Ori and the Blind Forest: DE is arguably the best metroidvania style game i have played in the last 5 years. Comparing against games such as Guacamelee, Shadow Complex, Axiom Verge, Dust and even to some extent Cave Story. This game is absolutley gorgeous, giving an oasis in the woods feel that makes you geniunely happy to play the game and explore new areas. Speaking of areas, i noticed one of the negative reviews touched on the lack of new content delivered in the Definitive Edition of the game, which mind you is correct. Black Root Burrows, with proper knowledge of the area can be traversed in under 10 minutes. However, something about the addition of an area solely focusing on the light and dark aspect of the world, rarely present in the main game, gives this area a totally unique feel and seems to fit perfectly with the original game. Instead of looking at this area as a new addition try and look at the definitive edition as just that, the way the game should be. I could just as easily say it took me 5 minutes to get to wall jump, does that area feel any less interesting or complete. Alright lets move on to the always present pros and cons.
PROS:
- The sound direction. This game has an beautiful and atmospheric soundtrack fit for the area the game takes place in.
- The movement. Oh god the movement. This is the reason i picked up this game as a speedrun and added it to my top ten games of all time. Every motion feels fluid, wall jumps that give that spiral animation are so damn satisfying. Ech ability gained always adds to that movement as well. I never felt like i got an ability and was overpowered in terms of travesing the world. Okay....maybe bash but....bash is super fun and can be used in such creative ways.
- The story. I won't go into it too much but goddamn what a tearjerker. nuff said
- The abilites. Each ability gained feels like a new tool in your aresenal, epanding your movement options to allow for more creative traversal. Not gonna spoil anything but just wait for bash, it will blow your mind.
- The CHEATCODE. okay, so for most this doesnt seem like a big deal and honestly it isnt much of one but if you hit left, up, right, down, up, up, up, jump, Ori will change into one of an infinite amount of colors adding some diversity to a character who is usually stark white. Idk its just cool and it brings me back to the old days of button combos on start screens to get cool effects.
- Sequence Breaking. im not spoiling anything but if you beat the game and are curious, go check out grimelios on youtube, very cool vids detailing sequence breaks and tricks in Ori.
CONS:
- The difficulty. While there are many settings in place to curb the difficulty this game is punishing as hell. If you explore and ge the health cells it will be a breeze but for those who like to rush through games, be careful. Its hard but not bad once you've learned the mechanics. nuff said.
- alright umm... im actually sitting here having a hard time coming up with more cons other than "its hard"
- i guess if i had to give another con, some areas you can progress really far in only to reach the ending and fins out you arent able to pass without a certain item. It happened to me twice but honestly at least you know how to get back there once you've gotten the item.
Sorry i went a little light on the cons, its honestly really hard for me to find something this game doesnt do well. the underwater sections are well paced and can be skipped entirely if you know what you are doing. The flying feels dynamic with the inclusion of the bash and the ending feels satisfying. Definitely give it a try if you are on the fence. Moon Studios has outdone themselves.

What are the nine scariest words in the English language? "We're Delta Force and we're here to save you!"
It's been four years since I played Spec Ops: The line. Since then it's lingered in my mind, occasionally taking me back and causing me to relive the horrors. Even now, I'm still not sure what genre to place it in. Action drama or action tragedy perhaps? Whatever genre it's in, I know this:
It's the number one of all time.
In some games, the only way to lose is when you turn the game off and stop playing. Here, it's the only way to win. And I strongly doubt many players have won. Your desire to finish, to see what comes next, is expertly pitted against your better judgement. Almost always the former prevails over the latter.
Of course, there are those harping on mediocre 2007 gameplay or shoehorned in multiplayer. I surmise that they have completely missed the point. It's like criticising a masterwork painting for being in a shoddy museum or having a dirty frame. This is doubly true because Spec Ops' message is about being in such a museum, poking fun at the box it comes in.
Poking fun is entirely the wrong word, so instead let's call it poking nauseated revulsion.
If you have a timemachine, go back to 2012 and tell yourself to play it. If you lack such a device, reading this review alone probably spoils too much. Part of the experience was going into it thinking it was Modern Warfare 2. The real reasons to play it now are academic, archeological. Also the soundtrack is pretty good.
Verdict: Recommended, perhaps above all to see what the hype was about.

Let me explain Hitman to you. In a simple way so it isn't confusing.
Hitman is a game where you are asked to assassinate a target. Sometimes two. Sometimes more. These targets do not want to die, obviously but they do not know they are about to. Your job is to be a literal grim reaper. Death can come in many shapes and sizes and the fun comes in finding out ways to kill your target. One day, it's a shot to the head. The next day, maybe they fall off a cliff. Some days, they suffer death from flesh eating virus or exploding rubber duck. Pretty much all you need to know is that the world is wide open, lots to see and do and it's a pleasure to play after how awful Absolution was.
The whole season is full of things to do. Not just the story mode stuff. Each map also contains escalation missions, which are missions that grow harder each time you do it by adding new targets, rules and stipulations to them. Every so often, a timed exclusive mission will come up too where you can earn some extra outfits for 47. Dressing him like some kind of weird murderous Ken doll (If Barbie is into that thing).
The only downside to the game is its always online connectivity. If you go offline, you lose all your progression and unlocks. This is kinda BS considering it shouldn't need to be online, but i guess it's to stop hackers and what-not. It's not an excuse, I'm just not personally bothered by things like that.
At the time of writing this, it's 50% off due to Black Friday. Get it. For that price, you are getting a chunk of game and Season 2 is due next year!

I've ignored Undertale for longest time. Its fandom was already running rampart, and ignoring their overexaggeration, I thought Undertale was some underwhelming and generic RPG with dull graphics. But... Not until I tried it myself. I thought I would not struggle. I thought I would not shed a single tear to a game. I thought I won't be impressed. I was all wrong... So wrong... Undertale is truly a great indie title, like nothing seen before. There needs to be more games like it.
Now let's go to PROS and CONS, shall we?
PROS:
-Fighting is (mostly) optimal. There will be many parts where its focused on alternative ways of defeating your foe without killing it. It's what makes the game unique. It requires you to be creative and think freely in decision making.
-RPG - RNG = Undertale; Fighting and dodging mechanics are fair and fun.
-Although visuals look simplistic and pixelated, they are not as limited as seen. Prepare to see impressive stuff.
-Interesting puzzles to solve. Even in fights, you have to figure out what is required to spare characters.
-Quite entertaining humor. Sometimes well-thought out, sometimes just small comedy things that makes us smile.
-Loveable characters whose biographies and backstories are scattered around the world.
-Replayability and different endings.
(Small) CONS:
-Although the game bases on choices, some can feel really lack-luster. For example, killing some characters won't affect too much to the game. Killing or sparing everyone you encounter, however, makes big differences.
-Hard-to-come-by choices. Some choices can't be uncovered without trial-and-error. Completely new players won't be able to take every tinniest detail in consideration that it will affect the fate of characters, and it can lead to fatal mistakes and unwanted choices. On brighter side, it adds up as a bonus to replayability.
-Sparing random encounters are very unrewarding and difficult. It's much easier to slay them, as its only way to gain EXP and increase max HP, which will be extremely helpful when wanting to spare major characters by tanking their attacks.
-Healing items have no limitations. Stacking on healing items will make fights easy, even better, when you can dodge majority of attacks. Even if you run out of healing items, the fights will be almost at end anyway.
-Bad currency balance and shops. Most of objects in shops can be found for free by exploring, and the OP healing items are really cheap, while the amount of gold you earn is rather big. Then, there are places that ask for way too much gold. I get that it's supposed to be a joke, but its been done more than once, it's not necessary.
-Useless items. Not counting the jokey ones, many items are just waste of gold and you can complete the game just fine without them. Some do have interesting concept (e.g. similar to in-battle stat buff items and berries from Pokemon), but, I never really seen a reason to buy and use them. Their upsides and downsides are all unbalanced. It's best to just stick to healing items.
Although seem like CONS are much bigger than PROS, but that's because constructive PROS might spoil fun. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND you try this game if you got money to spare, it can last +10 hours depending on how much you explore and/or replay, and it will turn your night into an unforgeable adventure. One more last thing: Don't let the game frighten you with its 4th wall breaking. Stay determined.

The first two hours of gameplay were already bad enough to make me wanna write a raging essay on how the CoD series has stopped evolving 7 years ago, but the game decided that it was time to give me the first real hardware issue I have ever had. Having to create new profiles for my BIOS and downclock my GPU to stock is some of the stupidest sh*t I have ever seen. I don't mind getting into hardware depths but that was just stupid. No response from Devs. and no real definitse solution I could find either.
The game. Black Ops II is no improvement from... Hell, it's a COD game. Modern Warfare 2 was a real step-up in atmosphere and story-telling, combined with one of the best multiplayers for its time and a real fun campaign; I still hear people talk about how harcore the Favella levels were when the game just came out. Modern Warfare 3 was basically the same game with some improved graphics and a new story with some very memorable moments(who doesn't know about the Eiffel Tower falling mission); Black Ops I was an interesting experience with some of the best characters and settings in the series to date. From there though, all following CoDs became "just CoDs". Easy to tell from the actual player reviews(and not the obviously paid-for IGN reviews) that Ghosts and Advanced Warfare are nothing spectacular.
Black Ops II isn't a terrible game. It's just not a step-up from the 60 bucks I spent on the last CoD half a year ago.

The narrative aspect of the game seems true to the dark character of Max and the tribal/feral/survival depths of the remains of humanity after whatever apacalyptic event sunk Australia into the depths we know and love from the movies.
The gameplay is generally very good. I would say the most similar game to Mad Max I have played is Far Cry 2, with Mad Max having less jungle and more desert, and with more driving and car customization. Much of the game is spent exploring the wasteland in your car, adding locations to your map and battling various wasteland gangs in the process. You spend most of the game helping various factions escape the iron boot of the big baddie of the game by taking down his various camps and building the resources of your allies. In doing so, you earn upgrades for Max and your super-car, improving your ability to fight hand-to-hand or on the road, respectively. You unlock various fast-travel points, as well, which reduces the amount of needless driving. (I drive over an hour a day to and from work; I don't necessarily want to spend my free time doing the same thing!)
The game's learning curve was fairly comfortable until you reach about the 90% point in the story and have to do the death race against the main henchman of the big baddie. Be warned: I found this race to be nearly impossible and no fun at all. I've read countless complaints from people on the web at how out-of-sync with the rest of the game the difficulty of this one encounter was, and I am in total agreement with those assessments. I had managed every possible upgrade to my car and vehicular weapons before attempting the race, and it was still absolute torture. Many players described how they managed quick-finishes to the race, but I could never manage it. I simply took try after try after try after try. It was work. It was frustrating, It was (in my opinion) very
poor game design. The entirety of the game leading up that encounter and following that encounter were fun - even really challenging in some parts - but that one race nearly overshadowed the rest of a very enjoyable game.

By far, this is one of the best shooters I’ve played. True enough, controls could have been better, but disregarding that, I loved it. We have the classic hero story, only that with each passing chapter it is continuously deconstructed. It appears that there truly exists a thin line between hero and villain, between good intentions and destruction. Visually, it is stunning and the evolution the characters undergo through the game, clothes, scars, are amazing. That is coupled with great lines during dialogue and also, changes made through it as the game progresses, from disciplined orders to outright shouting insults and screaming this orders. The game gradually gets more violent, but it does so to show the horrors of war, both experienced by the people around the war zones as those experienced by the same soldiers sent in to fight them.

This game's port is relatively solid, for the most part. It's stable, has a decent options menu with all the options this game really needs, the controller support is weird in the way that, when it is plugged in, every button prompt is replaced with the controller ones and you need to quit the game, unplug the controller and then start the game back up in order to get them back. This game didn't need an advanced options menu or magnificent control system or any of that♥♥♥♥♥♥ It's simple and it works. Normally I would complain about how simple it is but, like I said earlier, this game doesn't really need any of that. And I'll explain why later.
The graphics in this game are absolutely stunning. Beautiful shadows, incredible geometry, fantastic textures, awesome lighting effects, great particles, fantastic use of ambient occlusion and pretty good animation. It is a truly stunning game, but it isn't all that perfect. There are some weird textures here and there, weird models, animations and particles and some shadows look less than great, but it is both a visually stunning game and a visually pleasing game. The performance in this game is amazing too. It runs extremely well as my rig, an FX 4300 OC'd to 4.4 GHz and an EVGA GTX 750 ti, as it goes all over the place between 70 and 150 FPS maxed out. It really varies but it stays above 70 FPS all the time so that's awesome. Seriously fantastic job with this Yager.

I just finished playing Mad Max, and it was an overall really positive experience.
The narrative aspect of the game seems true to the dark character of Max and the tribal/feral/survival depths of the remains of humanity after whatever apacalyptic event sunk Australia into the depths we know and love from the movies.
The gameplay is generally very good. I would say the most similar game to Mad Max I have played is Far Cry 2, with Mad Max having less jungle and more desert, and with more driving and car customization. Much of the game is spent exploring the wasteland in your car, adding locations to your map and battling various wasteland gangs in the process. You spend most of the game helping various factions escape the iron boot of the big baddie of the game by taking down his various camps and building the resources of your allies. In doing so, you earn upgrades for Max and your super-car, improving your ability to fight hand-to-hand or on the road, respectively. You unlock various fast-travel points, as well, which reduces the amount of needless driving. (I drive over an hour a day to and from work; I don't necessarily want to spend my free time doing the same thing!)
The game's learning curve was fairly comfortable until you reach about the 90% point in the story and have to do the death race against the main henchman of the big baddie. Be warned: I found this race to be nearly impossible and no fun at all. I've read countless complaints from people on the web at how out-of-sync with the rest of the game the difficulty of this one encounter was, and I am in total agreement with those assessments. I had managed every possible upgrade to my car and vehicular weapons before attempting the race, and it was still absolute torture. Many players described how they managed quick-finishes to the race, but I could never manage it. I simply took try after try after try after try. It was work. It was frustrating, It was (in my opinion) very
poor game design. The entirety of the game leading up that encounter and following that encounter were fun - even really challenging in some parts - but that one race nearly overshadowed the rest of a very enjoyable game.

Spec Ops: The Line is an enjoyable third person shooter. The game mechanics are solid and as a result the cover-based shooting feels incredibly natural. Spec Ops is at its best when the fluid game movement is showcased in gorgeous action set pieces. The graphics are fantastic, this is as true in 2016 as it was at release. What truly puts Spec Ops above the run-of-the-mill third person action shooter is its story and disturbingly realistic depiction of  the brutalities of war. The story is based off of two other works: the novel, Heart of Darkness, and the classic film Apocalypse Now--which was also based off of Heart of Darkness. War and the decisions it forces humans to make are the heart of the story. The game is incredibly graphic, which the developers use in their favor. Not once did I think the game was graphic for the sake of being graphic. Each moment that incited shock felt horrifically natural and succeced in blurring the lines of morality--as war has done and will continue to do. A standard run through of the game will take around 10-15 hours, but that can be extended through collecting all of the Intel or playing on the unlockable FUBAR difficulty. All said and done, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Spec Ops: The Line. I definitely recommend checking it out especially if it's on sale. The multiplayer community is, for all intents and purposes, dead, which is to be expected at this point, so if you're looking to check that out it's not going to happen. The campaign, always the focus of the game, is strong enough on its own to leave any player satisfied even without the multiplayer.
TL;DR: Fantastic narrative, solid cover shooter, would recommend.

This game really took me by surprise. I was prepared to have a frustating experience due to the always online thing. But couldn't be more wrong. Yes, it sucks. Never had problem with it, but the mere fact that it exists is enough to live a sour taste in my mouth.
But, even then, I could not recommend this game based solely on that. HITMAN is amazing in every way. I get this Blood Money vibe everytime I play it. And it means a lot. If you want to confirm it, you just gotta ask to any fan of the Hitman series.
Anyway, (10 - Always Online) out of 10. Recommended.

Pros
- A return to the formula that made the series great. Open ended missions with top notch stealth mechanics allow creative solutions to eliminating your target.
- New content regularly produced be it new episodes (hears hoping for season 2) to challenges and time exclusive targets.
Cons
- There appears to be a problem with button prompts not always firing.
- The same actions will not always result in the same consequences.
- Always online DRM. This is a single player game always online just punishes people with a poor internet connection and that's assuming the servers have 100% uptime.
- Poor pricing, it's more expensive to purchase the intro pack and episodes separately than to buy the full game, punishing consumers for being informed. (may be specific to my region?)
Overall, I can't recommend Hitman, I can overlook the later two Cons but the former could be easily patched and seven months later they're still here. By and large the former two cons won't impact the casual player but if you try any of the timed challenges it could drive you to insanity which is a shame as it's an otherwise great game.

Hitman 2016 is in my opinion the best of the series, and that includes the much lauded Blood Money.
While it is true that it is not perfect, mostly due to a DRM scheme which is unnecessary at best and game-breaking at worst, I've gotten so many hours and so much entertainment out of the game that I can easily look past its shortcomings.
The levels are expansive and detailed, and this Hitman is the first game I've ever played where the "episodic" model has worked, mostly owing to the fact that the developers have been active and quick.
This game is worth full price, and is a steal at a sale price. Do yourself a favor and get the Full Experience!

A three paragraph review...
Borderlands 2 is exactly what it says it on the tin; Psychos, midget psychos, and a dusty dirty comic-book like setting that is unapologetic about it's juvenile and very bloody humor. The controls are well configured and the PC version allows for easy re-allocation of keys. The graphics are novel and overall the world has a very unique (and gritty cartoon) feel to it.
The good guns are hard to come by and farming is required. A lot of weapon stat reading should be expected if you want good results but the stats themselves are fairly self explanatory. The first third of the game is a bit of a grind and the humor can be abrasive if fart jokes and shooting nut-bag crazies in the head over and over gets old for you. I enjoyed the game a great deal (I guess I am easy to please), Borderlands 2 is easy to play and required very little focus to enjoy. Overall I recommend it to anyone looking for a quick easy laugh  and a straightforward co-op shooter to have a good time with.
It bears mentioning that there is a huge amount of down-loadable content and that the replay value is very high. The only major difficulty I have had with this game, and many others have as well is that it is very easy to get too many levels before you have run through all of the content that you want to play. Of course, it also bears mentioning that this is precisely the reason the replay value is so high. Try it out, it is a lot of fun!

Spec Ops: The Line is an enjoyable third person shooter. The game mechanics are solid and as a result the cover-based shooting feels incredibly natural. Spec Ops is at its best when the fluid game movement is showcased in gorgeous action set pieces. The graphics are fantastic, this is as true in 2016 as it was at release. What truly puts Spec Ops above the run-of-the-mill third person action shooter is its story and disturbingly realistic depiction of  the brutalities of war. The story is based off of two other works: the novel, Heart of Darkness, and the classic film Apocalypse Now--which was also based off of Heart of Darkness. War and the decisions it forces humans to make are the heart of the story. The game is incredibly graphic, which the developers use in their favor. Not once did I think the game was graphic for the sake of being graphic. Each moment that incited shock felt horrifically natural and succeced in blurring the lines of morality--as war has done and will continue to do. A standard run through of the game will take around 10-15 hours, but that can be extended through collecting all of the Intel or playing on the unlockable FUBAR difficulty. All said and done, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Spec Ops: The Line. I definitely recommend checking it out especially if it's on sale. The multiplayer community is, for all intents and purposes, dead, which is to be expected at this point, so if you're looking to check that out it's not going to happen. The campaign, always the focus of the game, is strong enough on its own to leave any player satisfied even without the multiplayer.
TL;DR: Fantastic narrative, solid cover shooter, would recommend.

i know i gave this game a thumbs up but never in my life have i been so...torn when it comes to my enjoyment of a game like this.
there are things i like in sister location and there are things i don't like in sister location, i guess i'll start with the good.
PROS: this is the most story driven game in the fnaf series and is a huge leap forward and i like that, the previous fnaf games told their stories through 8-bit mini games and/or secret newspaper clipings which left most of the story unclear but in sister location tells the story clearly, now some story bits are still left in the dark but not as much as in the past games.
the robot designs in sister location are just amazing, scott was always good at making robots and sister location shows off his best work from the highly detailed looks of circus baby and ballora to the simple, yet refined looks of bidybab and minireena to the nice redesigns of freddy, bonnie, and foxy
ok now i talk about the things i don't like in sister location.....
CONS: the gameplay, in the first 3 fnaf games, they had camera and power management mechanics and in fnaf4, it had sound based mechanics and all previous games, each one of the 5 nights got harder and harder but in sister location...it's basicly a diffrent minigame each night with story bits in between
night 1: tutorial night
night 2: hide and seek with bidybab and red light, green light with ballora and freddy
night 3: hide and seek with foxy and bonnie
night 4: i'll talk about night 4 in my next point.......
night 5: follow the leader with circus baby
i found most of these nights to be vary boring and tedious and i only sloged through them to get to the next part of the story.
final con.....night 4, it's easily the worst part of the game, at night 4 you get stuffed in a springlock suit and have to keep the springlocks from getting lose while fending off minirenna, sounds okay on paper...till you actually play it
1: there are too many springlocks to keep track of, this wouldn't be so bad if not for minirenna
2: every time minirenna grabs on to you, you have to shake it off causing the springlocks to get lose faster and due to the high number of springlocks, you get overwelmed fast and end up losing the night
3: everytime you die, you have to sit through a 5 min. cutscene...and you can't skip it
4: even though scott made the night easier in a recent patch, it's still frustrating to play
and well..that's it for the review, overall i wanted to enjoy the game and i'm happy scott is willing to change things up, this was a poor exucution and still needs some work but for something i paid $8 for...i guess it could of been worse
(scott announced a custom night update to the game that will be released in december, when it comes out i will update my review to share my thoughts on it)

Super Meat Boy is the best platformer to come out in over a decade. The game is HARD. But never unfair. The controls are so tight that if you ever die then it’s your own fault and not just a cheap shot that the game took. The instant respawn is also so smooth that you never get frustrated for too long as you will be back to giving the stage one more shoot. After a couple of times you discover something magical happening to you, you are blitzing through the part that took you so long to pass even 5 minutes ago. It gets programmed into your muscle memory so well that you can do the begining of the stage with your eyes closed. It’s the first time I have experienced something like this and I kept coming back to the sadistic level designs. No matter how impossible the stage looks in the beginning, through trial and error and instant respawning, one would unknowingly master the stage and never get stuck in it.The music in the game is also very catchy. You can listen to them for hours and not get bored of it, and then later catch yourself humming it unintentionally. There are 7 worlds with roughly 20 stages each, with each having a dark counterpart stage to it that’s harder. Plus with the introduction of “Teh Internets” now the community can make and share their stages as well, making the number of stages infinite. There are also unlockable characters from other indie game that have different moves then meat boy. In conclusion, Super Meat Boy is a game that keeps on giving and is a MUST HAVE for people who want a challenging platformers with the tightest controls that ever was.

Some tables are entirely foldable for easy transportation, e.g., camping. This game was initially disappointing, with Square Enix announcing episodic releases of content in DLC form. For its original price and what was available in the Prologue and Episode 1, there was an underwhelming amount of gameplay for what was essentially a promise from the studio. With the recent release of the complete first season, however, I do feel that Hitman has evolved to become a game that none of the previous Hitman games could ever be: a professional assassin simulator that truly made you feel like a professional assassin.
Each episode in the game is effectively a large puzzlebox with any number of solutions. By encouraging replay through challenges and "elusive target" missions, your knowledge of the map, timing, and opportunities make you feel like you have truly cased the location, creating gameplay that would not be possible if you were seeing everything for the first time. The feeling of badass-ed-ness when you cleanly execute a string of assassinations only to slip away unnoticed, all thanks to prior knowledge of the map is incredibly fulfilling, and is exactly the experience of the built in "escalation" missions.
The game has its technical faults as others have mentioned, such as the always-online DRM. The ambient conversation can also be jarring as everyone in the game sounds "American", though the episodes each clearly feature cities that have cultural associations. Beyond these issues, however, the gameplay itself is great and definitely deserves a playthrough, even if only to explore the beautiful sandboxes that Square Enix has created.

Endless replayability is the name of the game here, with dozens of assassinations, oppurtunities and unique ways to mess up someone's day in each level, of which there are 6. Oh and also the 2 bonus levels. And the tutorial I spent 10 hours enjoying. And the ~10 escalation missions for each level. And the user-created contracts. And Spelunky-daily style Elusive Targets. I honestly wish I'd picked this up closer to release so I had more time to enjoy each level as they came out. Possibly my GOTY 2016 for innovating on episodic releases.

The Ubi in Ubisoft also stands for ubi-quitous. Ubisoft's games follow the same rinse-and-repeat pattern of quest, some form of viewpoint that reveals map markers, collect-a-thon to level up your character, quest, repeat.
WB have followed this same pattern, but where Shadow of Mordor had the excellent Nemesis system, and the Batman games had ♥♥♥♥ing Batman, the Mad Max games have several shades of brown and yellow and driving.
Now, this game is fun. The driving combat is cool. The hand-to-hand combat is boring as sin though. The game itself has cool moments but I keep getting pulled back to the ubiquitous Ubisoft formula. Get in a hot air balloon to reveal map markers. Raid a camp for scrap. Spend scrap on levelling-up the car or Max. Quest. Repeat.

First two acts are fantastic; the third gets very grindy and it's difficult to stay immersed, a la any Assassin's Creed game, which I would compare this game favorably to. That said, it's still a great game for the $3 price tag that I bought it with, and would recommend it to anybody that is a fan of the post apocalyptic setting.
Edit: Also, be prepared for one of the more polarizing endings I've ever experienced. I'm still trying to decide what my opinion of it really is.

Everyone seems to love this game, but it just didn't come together into an enjoyable package for me.
The introductory sequence (about 20 minutes or so) made a very poor first impression. The movement during the "interactive" opening is painfully slow, and the attempts to get me emotionally attached to the characters were not effective.
I stopped caring about the story here at the beginning, and nothing thereafter made me re-engage.
The few characters who speak in this game use a synthetic language. The little sprite that follows you around is cute, and has a lot of variety in his/her different sounds. The problem is the deep-voiced narrator. From the intonation of his phrases to the individual pronunciation of syllables, he sounds exactly like Jabba the Hutt. No joke, it is either an intentional homage or the creators were unaware of the influence of Return of the Jedi when they thought they were creating original sounds. It is very distracting and you can't take anything he says seriously.
The combat is unsatisfying and consists primarily of mashing a single attack button when you are somewhat near an enemy. This is because attacks auto-target foes; you don't even have to be facing them. Fortunately combat is not a major part of the game.
The music seems good at first, but most zones are quite large, with the corresponding music tracks on a relatively short loop, and they get old fast. The artwork and animations are beautiful, no problem there.
Don't let the colorful palette and cute characters fool you; a handful of sequences are extraordinarily difficult. These catch you off guard because the majority of the game is very forgiving as far as the basic platforming and combat goes. Then every so often (
) you will hit sections where the spikes in the challenge level are abrupt and extreme, where you will be required to exhibit near-perfect timing and repeat long sections over and over until you get everything right. The game was reminiscent of something like Super Meat Boy at these times. I have a hunch that many people enjoyed the game up until
, and that was the end for them.
Platforming and exploration follow the Metroidvania style where you find power-ups that expand your techniques for moving about the world. But a lot of the treasures you can backtrack to get aren't really worth it (too many of them are just experience globes) and there is really only one main path forward as you gain each new ability.
There are some cool stages in this game, like the one where certain parts of the floor and walls will rotate the orientation of your directional movement and jumps. It's hard to explain and best experienced on your own. That is, if you can make it past
. :)
